SafeSport

The PanAm Championships and DCCX organizing committee support the goals of SafeSport in protecting athletes and ensuring a positive environment for athletes, supporters and fans. 

Implementation of SafeSport protocols is the responsibility of the officiating crew. No person listed on the SafeSport Centralized Disciplinary Database is permitted in the pit area or team zones. Please provide the names of pit staff during check in (if different from staff you listed when registering). For non-U.S. support staff, a cycling federation license is required. Please present names of support staff and license numbers (if applicable) at registration. Specific questions about SafeSport guidelines pertaining to your support staff can be directed to the UCI or USA Cycling official in charge of pit pass allocation.

Licensing Requirements: All riders competing in the Pan American Championships, Masters Pan American Championships, and/or UCI C2 races must possess a current UCI International license.

If you currently do not hold a license of any kind the UCI license for an adult is $240.

If an athlete currently holds a USA Cycling domestic license, then you are able to purchase a UCI license add-on at a cost of $130 (the price difference between a USA Cycling license and the fee for a UCI license). You are eligible to purchase this add-on up to 30 days prior to an existing USA Cycling membership expiring. Per USA Cycling: this UCI license supersedes a domestic license and thus your domestic license will show as expired once the UCI license add-on is purchased.

The UCI/International license is valid for both UCI categorized races and any local/grassroots races.

More details available here: https://usacycling.org/get-started/bike-racing-for-adults

All riders in the DCCX amateur races must possess either a valid USAC license, a one-day USAC license or a UCI license with cyclocross coding. Non-US citizens must possess a valid UCI International license for insurance purposes. Non-US citizens from Canada can possess a Cycling Canada License.*

*If registering with a license from Canada is not an international (UCI) license, then applicable riders will be required to show proof of insurance that covers them while racing in the USA or sign a waiver acknowledging responsibility for all medical costs they may incur. USA Cycling's insurance does NOT cover riders with only valid domestic licenses from their respective national federation. Foreign federation UCI licenses are to carry with them proper medical insurance, but a Foreign Permission Letter (FPL) is required for it to be in effect. If no FPL is available, the rider is responsible for obtaining travel insurance that covers them while racing in the USA, and they accept full responsibility for medical expenses they incur.

Masters Pan American Championship Eligibility

All riders who hold a current masters UCI license and UCI ID may ride in the Masters Pan American championships. However, the following riders are not eligible for the Masters Championship:

  1. Any rider who has ridden in the UCI cyclocross World Championships (Elite), Continental Championships, or UCI cyclocross World Cup during the current cyclocross season.
  2. Any rider, who has been a member, during the current cyclocross season, of a team registered with the UCI.
  3. Any rider classified with at least 100 points in the UCI individual cyclocross ranking published after the first UCI cyclocross world cup event of the current cyclocross season.

Note Regarding USA Cycling restrictions on Masters racers for USA National Championship events:

Any Masters racer who “Has a racing age of 30 years or older and has competed in any elite UCI World Cups, World Championships, Pan American Championship, Pan American or Olympic Games within the current calendar year MUST enter their respective Elite category.” 

 

Start Order and Start Procedures

Saturday

Feeding:

USAC Rule 4A15: Feeding is generally not permitted unless specifically authorized by the Chief Referee. If authorized, there is normally no feeding in the first two and final two laps of the race, and a temperature of at least 68 degrees is recommended. The location of feeding will be determined by the Chief Referee in conjunction with the Race Organization.

course or outside the designated area. UCI 5.1.063

Local Food & Services Guide

On behalf of DCMTB, Crosshairs Cycling, and CXD Trek Bikes - Welcome to Washington DC! We are excited to be hosting the PanAmerican Cyclocross Championships and DCCX at the Armed Force Retirement Home. 

 

This city and region are great places to live, ride, and race. Check out this photo essay in the Radavist from friend of DCCX, Andy Karr of the Great Eskape, for more about the cycling communities and events in the city (including DCCX) that make this place special!

 

One of the biggest questions that bike racers and teams have when they come from out of town to a race and venue is where places to get food and groceries are located. This guide will direct you to places to eat and drink, nearby grocery stores close to the race venue, as well as the food trucks that will be at the venue so that racers, teams, supporters, and attendees can plan accordingly. 

 

We are grateful to be sponsored once again by Right Proper Brewing! We will be selling their beer at the race. Right Proper has two locations in DC - the Brookland Tasting Room and Right Proper Kitchen. Both Brookland locations are just a few minutes from the race venue and the new Right Proper Kitchen location in the Brookland ArtsWalk features a large outdoor patio perfect for hanging out after the racing is done!

 

Zeke’s Coffee of DC has been a longtime DCCX sponsor and we are happy to have them back as a sponsor as well as vendor for both days of racing. Visit them at their Rhode Island Ave NE Roastery/Coffee Shop or make the quick trip over to their Uptown Coffee Shop, less than a mile and a half from the race venue on 14th Street NW. If you land on a podium you might even take home a bag of Zeke's special DCCX Race Fuel coffee!

 

Acme Pie has been the official pie of DCCX for as long as we can remember! They have been a sponsor and a vendor for many years. Sol will be back once again this year serving pie to the hungry masses. Stop by the shop on Columbia Pike in Arlington VA if you are in town for an extra day to take pie home. 

 

We will have a number of food trucks on site during the race weekend. Below is the list of days and times they will be available:

  • TeaLoveBoba - Handcrafted drinks, including milk teas, fruits teas, and lemonade. Sat from 11am-4pm, Sun from 10am-5pm
  • TNT Mexican Grill -  Authentic Mexican street food including breakfast tacos. All day on Sat and Sun
  • Kush - Local cyclist Chef Ali’s unique Sudanese/Middle Eastern food truck. Sat and Sun after 11am
  • Blue Nile Burgers - Chef Ali’s take on classic burgers and loaded fries. Sun after 11am. 

 

Grocery Stores:

Safeway-Petworth - walking distance (¼ mile) to the venue on Georgia Ave. Open til midnight. Has a pharmacy. 

Yes Organic Market - like a smaller Whole Foods about half mile from the venue. 

Giant-Columbia Heights - a bit further (1.5 miles) but still close. Has a pharmacy. 

Trader Joes-Brookland - just opened, 2 miles from venue (1 hr free parking in garage on 8th St)

All above stores sell beer and wine.

 

Other services:

Two hardware stores nearby

  • Petworth ACE Hardware - less than a mile from the venue. 
  • Annie’s ACE Hardware - about 2 miles from the venue, near Trader Joe’s. 

CVS Pharmacy - on Georgia Ave about a half mile from the venue. 

Walmart - two Supercenters nearby if you need any last minute tents/race supplies:

  • Riggs Rd NE (just under 2 miles)
  • Georgia Ave NW (just over 2 miles)

Target-Columbia Heights - near the Giant, less than 2 miles from the venue in the DC USA complex. 

Georgia Ave/Petworth Metro station is at 3700 Georgia Ave NW Washington DC 20010, half mile walk or bike from the venue.

Loyalty Bookstore - one of the best local bookstores, just down the street at 9th and Upshur St NW. Open all weekend. 

Monroe Street Farmers Market at the Brookland Arts Walk. Sat from 9am-1pm. 2 miles from the race venue near Trader Joe’s, right next to the Brookland Metro (Red Line) and Met Branch Trail. 

 

Local Bike Shop & Ride Guide

We are thankful to be sponsored by Trek Bikes! We greatly appreciate Trek Clarendon (Arlington, VA) for providing neutral support for the race weekend. Go see Jeff Fraley and his team if you need service or parts before your big race. There are other Trek shops in the region -  check this list to find out where the closest Trek shop is if Trek Clarendon is not convenient.  There are two Trek stores in DC proper, Trek Skyland and Trek Georgetown.  

 

Arrow Bicycle in Hyattsville, MD, is about 5 miles from the race venue. They are a Trek dealer and are located along the Rhode Island Avenue Trolley Trail, near the Anacostia River Trail. An easy ride from the race venue!

 

There are two community bike shops within a few miles of the race venue. Highly recommended to stop in and learn more about what they do and grab a tube or any last minute bicycle need:

 

Gearin Up is a project of the Washington Area Bicyclist Association located in the Eckington neighborhood in NE DC, right off the Metropolitan Branch Trail (MBT). They are open until 7pm on Fridays and noon to 6pm on Saturdays. 

Upshift Workshop is an eclectic, woman-owned bicycle repair and education workshop in the Adams Morgan neighborhood in NW DC. They are open until  7pm on Fridays and noon-4pm on Saturdays and Sundays. 

 

If you are staying in the host hotel in the NoMA neighborhood, you’re just around the corner from DC’s flagship REI , adjacent to the NoMA Metro station (Red Line) and abutting the Metropolitan Branch Trail.

 

There are tons of places to ride in DC! The District Department of Transportation has a bicycle map that is worth looking at to familiarize yourself with bike lanes and trails in the city. You can find that map here.

 

Other places to ride:

The Metropolitan Branch Trail (MBT) is a multi-use trail that runs through the center of Washington, DC, connecting Union Station to (eventually) Silver Spring, MD. Most of the 8 miles are complete and there are protected bike lanes most of the way from the race venue to the trail access point in the Brookland neighborhood. Here are directions to the trail/two way protected cycletrack - hang a left at 8th St NE/Arts Walk to go up towards MD, hang a right to head downtown and Union Station. 

 

The Anacostia River Trail network starts in Maryland and continues into Washington, DC. Most of it is paved though there are sections of the NW Branch Trail that are dirt/singletrack (and perfect for cyclocross bikes if you like climbing). For info on the DC side, go here. For MD info, go here. 

 

Going for a bicycle ride in Rock Creek Park has been part of DC cycling life for decades. Junior World Road Championships were hosted there in 1978! This World Championship event was the first hosted in the US since 1912! If you want to relive that event, and see if you can better Greg LeMond’s 9th place finish, the race route is here.

 

North of Broad Branch Rd, much of Beach Drive is closed to car traffic so it is a great place to ride and explore. Only about two miles from the race venue is the Morrow Drive entrance to Rock Creek Park (at the Fitzgerald Tennis Center). At Beach Drive, make a right to head north towards Maryland and a left to head south towards Broad Branch and the Rock Creek trail which heads towards Georgetown and the National Mall (monuments, museums etc)

 

Sligo Creek Parkway has multiple road sections closed off to cars during the weekend, as well as a parallel multi-use trail. A great place to ride if you are staying north of DC in Silver Spring or Wheaton. More about Sligo Creek here. 

 

A bit further west are the paved Capital Crescent Trail and the unpaved C & O Canal Towpath. Both start in DC, in the Georgetown neighborhood, and meander into Maryland. 

 

DC does have legal singletrack! And cyclocross bikes fare pretty well on these trails. Learn more about the Ft Dupont and Ft Circle Park trails here. 

Last but not least is a favorite for those of us that live in the NE part of the city and Prince George’s County - the Beltsville Agricultural Research Center and the Patuxent Research Refuge. Miles of relatively low traffic roads. Take the Rhode Island Avenue Trolley Trail north and connect to Beaver Dam Rd and head east. Here are directions from the race venue.

EventName: Bison or Bust! The Tertiary Trek: National Bison Day Ride to Midewin National Tallgrass Prairie
EventNotes:
Public & Free

Hear Ye Hear Ye By way of bipartisan act of Congress and signed by President Obama into federal law, National Bison Day will be henceforth observed the first Saturday of every November! To celebrate this momentous occasion of the newly-dubbed “National Mammal” join a glorious mixed road & light gravel ride to a bison herd / obstinacy at Midewin National Tallgrass Prairie.

“Bison or Bust! The Tertiary Trek”
This remix of our inaugural 2024 ride is on the preserve’s 30th anniversary, for which they domesticated their roughest gravel segment. Lunch orders will be delivered to the bison preserve’s welcome center. Rendezvous include Metric Coffee (All), Blackberry Market (A & B), Jitters Cafe (All), Midewin Welcome Center (All), and The Junction vintage shop (All) for the after party. Everyone returns same-day to LaSalle St. Station by a specially-reserved Metra car. Before Joliet, anyone starting with “A” group can switch to “B” by just waiting. Everyone can switch to any other group at Jitters in Joliet, as well as the Midewin Welcome Center. Join our Strava club for updates!
 

“What are the ride rules?”

  • DO NOT PET THE FLUFFY COWS!
  1. All participants read, understand, and agree to the release / disclaimer / waiver at the bottom of the site before joining the ride
  2. Helmets required strapped onto your noggin’
  3. Bring a front and rear taillight as well as the tools, supplies, and know-how to change their own flats and address any mechanicals they may experience. From the 15th to 30th of October Comrade Cycles is offering free bike safety checks for our ride participants so get a checkup before the ride to cruise worry-free
  4. Observe best ride etiquette at all times: call out all slowing, stopping, speed bumps, holes, doors, cars, riders, runners, walkers, kids, turns, mechanicals, flats, gaps, and especially any pursuing buffaloes
  5. Keep your hands on your handlebars at all times, so flap your wings for rough roads instead of pointing. No riding without hands, we are too close together, roads are too unpredictable, and we have too far to go!
  6. Keep your eyes on the shoulders of the rider in front of you. They’ll call out and relay hazards as well as take the best line between them.
  7. That means if the rider ahead of you hits that minor road hole or whatever you do too, because it’s better than erratic unpredictable riding. No twitchy, racey, or unsafe group riding. There are plenty of other opportunities in other groups for that.
  8. No zooming in-between riders in peloton to make it three riders wide. Two wide? Stay that way. Single file? stay that way. It’s not a race, no need to jockey for position, and we will ask people to leave if they risk other riders’ safety
  9. Good vibes only! *All with good vibes are welcome* no matter their color shade, class, age, gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, profession, abilities, biking expertise, and strength.
  10. Good vibes only! That means no threatening or chauvinistic behavior of any kind is allowed be it racism, sexism, homophobia, classism, ethnic supremacism, or other forms of prejudice, threats, cruelty, or hatred nor are members of such ideologies permitted.
  11. No dangerous behavior is allowed and participants must follow all safety instructions of their ride leaders
  12. No unsolicited ‘coaching’ is allowed, especially any ‘helpful pushes’
  13. No triathlon aero handlebars are allowed they’re too unstable for the peloton
  14. No headphones
  15. Rides A and B require drop bars or something convincingly equivalent, like bullhorns. Point being that hybrid, flat, swoop, bull moose, albatross, wet noodle, whatever supercool other handlebars are only allowed for C group. This is just for safety in a peloton.
  16. No darting between riders. Is the peloton two riders wide? Keep it that way. Is it single-file? Keep it that way. Stay in your lane and ride with predictable behavior. This is not a race and anyone riding in ways that endanger others will be asked to find another ride.
  17. Join The ride Group appropriate for your abilities based on both practice and distance. Generally speaking, if you’ve been riding that distance in a week you’re ready to ride it in a day.
  18. Veteran brakeless fixed gear riders welcome but behind the peloton so pedal strikes don’t wipe others out.
  19. XXAndrew MichalskiXX or any other saboteurs

“What group should I join?”

For both Nachusa and Midewin routes the chillest group rolls at party pace, approximately 14mph, for around 40 miles. Both Midewin and Nachusa have a "B" group rolling for about 87 miles at 16-20mph once rolling. Both Midewin and Nachusa have an “A” group rolling at 18-24mph for about 130 miles. Whatever pace and distance you ride in a week you should able to do it in a day if you prepare well. Please practice riding in groups, calling out obstacles and "slowing" or "stopping" (see ride rules).

No groups are true drop rides. However, on “A” group we have a lot of miles to cover before dusk so if you have a really bad mechanical more involved than a flat, we must ask that you either link up with the next group riding by (when possible) or catch up at the next rendezvous by taking a shorter break to depart with us again. Study the routes and tabs atop the Ride With GPS event page carefully to make your choice. Keep in mind the ride is planned to be very adjustable:

  • Midewin Routes
    • Until Joliet, you can downgrade from "A" group by just waiting for "B" group.
    • You can change to any group at Jitters cafe in Joliet, and at the Midewin visitor's center.
    • Midewin Routes
      • Until Joliet we ride decently close to the train lines for the Heritage Corridor Metra train, but please keep in mind it does not run on weekends, and National Bison Day is always on the first Saturday of November. If you find yourself bonking your ejection seat lies on the Lincoln Service train home from Summit or Joliet, Carl Sandberg or Illinois Zephyr train home from La Grange, or in a ride share to the nearest Rock Island line Metra station, a line which begins at Joliet Gateway Station.

“What’s the timetable?”

TBA

“Do you have a waiver?”

Riding in groups and on roadways is extremely dangerous. Serious bodily injury and death can occur even when you and those around you are exercising extraordinary care. You must ride at your own risk. Thank you for being careful! By joining any of our rides all cyclists hereby release ride organizers, agents, sponsors, advertisers, partners, volunteers, affiliates and all other persons and entities from all liability. (Thanks Breakfast Club ATX!)

EventName: NICA Discovery- Warren, NJ Fall session 1
EventNotes:
We are so excited for your child to participate in NICA Discovery! 

 

All NICA Discovery adult leaders are background checked and hold a coaching license from NICA.  There will always be at least 2 leaders who have current first aid training. 

 

New Friends is the introductory level and is aimed at children who are new to biking but have some limited experience with neighborhood or urban riding.  These are children who can already balance and pedal a bike, but may have never ventured “off road.” Games and activities work on learning to better ride and operate a bike preparation for later buildable skills, and increasing stamina. 

 

Participants must be able to ride a bike without training wheels before joining a program and must be in 7-11 years old by program start date.

 

This session of NICA Discovery, Warren, NJ meets Saturdays 9:00 am-10:30

September 12

October 3

October 10

October 17

October 24

November 7

 

Required Documentation

ONLINE: 

  • Registration for NICA Discovery is through the platform BikeReg.  Go to bikereg.com and search “NICA Discovery” to find your location. 

IN PERSON: 

  • Parents must print, review this CODE OF CONDUCT with their child, sign and bring it to the first session for their child to participate. 
  • Every rider is also required to have a waiver and medical release form signed on file with NICA.  A link to the waiver may be found HERE.  Parents are asked to show confirmation that the online waiver has been signed before their child participates. 

Required Equipment

  • Helmet - Helmets should be less than 5 years old with no visible cracks or defects and fit your child’s head well without moving around while they ride. 
  • Footwear - Closed-toe (non-Croc like) shoes that fastened by laces, straps or buckles
  • Bike - Bike with knobby tires, gears, and two hand brakes. Bike tires should be no smaller than 20 inches.
  • Bike repair items - A replacement tube that fits your child’s tire. (dropped off at day one check in and returned at close of program if they are un-used.
  • Snug fitting small backpack  - Kids need to be able to carry water and snacks with them at all times.
  • Snacks/Hydration - Kids should always bring a snack and hydration with them to Discovery. 
    • Examples could include a granola bar, fruit snacks, or something that can easily be stored in a pocket or pack.
    • Hydration should consist of non caffeinated sports drinks or just good ole water! 

Recommended Equipment

  • Gloves - full-finger gloves to protect hands from abrasions in the case of a fall
  • Eye protection - generic sports glasses to protect from dust and debris (and bugs) kicked up while riding
  • Windbreaker /rain jacket/coat - weather conditions change throughout the season, your child should be prepared to ride in the conditions that are present on the day. Sessions will be altered or canceled if the weather conditions are unsafe. 
  • Athletic /Cycling pants- Loose fitting athletic pants. Cycling specific shorts are not required but some kids may be more comfortable.

What to Expect

Each lesson is broken down into 3 sections.  

  • Opener activities and objective/expectation setting
  • Skills activities and Games 
  • Wrap up and Reflection

There will be a  break mid-lesson for snacking/hydrating and general check in.

Each lesson builds on skills learned in the previous one.  To get the MOST out of NICA Discovery make sure your child can attend every lesson! 

For New Friends, the lessons consist of riding and playing in a park-like setting and are not trail dependent. Students will ride within that open space rather than out on trails, staying close to restroom facilities and support. 

 

Kids should come ready to learn, play, ride and explore!

Backpack examples 

A small pack that fits snugly and is just big enough to carry a water bottle and snacks, and maybe a small found treasure or two is great.

Helmet examples

Bike examples

How to determine if the bike is the correct size

Here is a statement regarding e-bike rules and regulations for the Threat Level Midnight Event:

Threat Level Midnight Event: E-Bike Rules and Regulations

To address inquiries regarding e-bike eligibility for the bike categories at the Threat Level Midnight Event, we are following the basic rules adopted by USA Cycling for competitive electric bicycle events.

The electric bikes permitted for competition are defined as Pedelecs" (pedal electrics), which utilize both pedaling and electric power.

For the Threat Level Midnight Event, we are adopting the Class 1 e-bike definition as the standard for entry. This ensures fair and regulated competition and aligns with the Consumer Products Safety Council guidelines:

Class 1 E-Bike Requirements:

No Throttle: The bike must not have a throttle mechanism.
Pedaling System:Must have a freely operable pedaling system (rear-wheel drivetrain of pedals, crank, chain, and gear system).
Motor Power:750 watts or less motor power (manufacturer's label of compliance is the minimum standard).
Motor Engagement: Motor assistance engages only when the rider is actively pedaling.
Motor Cut-Off: Motor assistance cuts off at a maximum speed of 20 mph (32 km/h).

Additional Allowable Options:

Battery: A single battery is permitted.
Start Assist: Limited start assist (without pedaling) is allowed up to a maximum speed of 4 mph (6 km/h).

Participants are responsible for ensuring their e-bike meets these specifications prior to the event. Compliance checks will be made. We look forward to seeing you at the start line!

 

Events are subject to weather and trail conditions. Helmets must be worn at all times while riding. Promoter reserves the right to cancel/reschedule the event. Promoter reserves the right to change start times and distances if needed. For more info or questions please email: events@missourioffroadcyclists.com

 

Funds raised go to support the Missouri Off Road Cyclists, a regional non-profit advocating for, building, maintaining, and preserving sustainable multi-use soft surface trails throughout Southwest Missouri.

EventNotes:
The Campus Cycling Collective, Inc. is proud to present The Rust Belt Ruckus! — A Buffalo Cyclocross Series

***Early bird pricing now until 9/15/2026 at midnight***

Adult Race Entry $40 -> $45 (after 9/15)

Adult 5 Race Series Entry $160  -> $185 (after 9/15)

Register early and save some hand up money!

**There will be day of reg at every event (cash only and $10 extra)**

*Individual Race Registrations are linked below*

Junior and U19 racers are encouraged to apply for our new limited

CCC Race Fee Scholarship : Fill Out This Form!

Overview

Back for 2026 your Buffalo cyclocross promoters have joined forces with the Campus Cycling Collective to bring you a better cyclocross season. The Rust Belt Ruckus will consist of a 5 race series in a condensed season format going from October 11th to November 15th. (no more August 80 degree cross race followed by weeks of no local races) All races will be UNSANCTIONED, meaning you do not need a USAC license to participate, or worry about one day licenses. This removes barriers of entry for Canadians, former license holders who miss riding in the tape, and new racers. 

We will have consistent race schedules and a condensed “Siuta” format so the entire day fits into 3 ½ hours of racing. This will put more people on the course at once making it more fun, not a solo time trial. This also gets you back to your family or allows plenty of hang out time or to help set/clean up the course. 

Each race will have its own podiums and awards, but at the final race on November 15th at One O Four Farm's Gobble OOF CX, we will present series awards for those who participated and performed the most & best & worst,  along with some other CX Promoter picked superlatives…. You must complete 4 races to be included in series awards/results.

Event Schedule

The Rust Belt Ruckus consists of 5 independent cross races. The races take place in October and November across the WNY region. You may sign up for the entire 5 race series on this page (and save $40!). Or you can sign up for individual races using the links below.

  • 10/11/26 - Knox Farm CX (East Aurora) Race One
  • 10/25/26 - OOFF CX (Lockport) Race Two
  • 11/1/26 - Beaver CX (Grand Island) Race Three
  • 11/8/26 - JR West Falls CX (West Falls) Race Four
  • 11/15/26 - Gobble OOF CX (Lockport) Race Five & Series Finale

Adults race all 5 races for $160 (plus fees). For juniors it's only $60 (plus fees) 

These are the early bird fees. After 9/15/26 Adults registration increases to $185. 

You can add a second race at EVERY race for an extra $60 ($15x4 one free).

 

Race Day Schedule

  • 9:30 am Registration Opens
  • 10:30 am Race One: Juniors u15 (on a shortened course)
  • 11:30 am Race Two: Cat 4/5, SS, Women Open, Women 4/5
  • 1:00 pm Race Three: Open 1/2/3/4/5, Cat ¾ Men 1:15 pm: Masters 40+, 50+, 60+, 70+
  • Race Podiums will be done after each race.
  • At Race 5 / Series Finale, all podiums will be done at the end. This includes race and series level podiums.

Series Rules

The series consists of 5 races, but only 4 results are required for overall series rankings. We don't want a single mechanical to ruin your overall ranking. 

4 results required to be eligible for series rankings and awards. 

If you complete all 5 races, the worst result will be discarded.

 

If you sign up for the whole series you only need to register ONCE (on this page).  You will receive a discount that equates to ONE FREE RACE. And you will SUPPORT all of us Buffalo cyclocross promoters who stick our necks out & volunteer our time. All with an end goal of getting to rode around a field like we are all 12 years old, with you, having the time of our lives…

 

So, what are you waiting for? Sign up today and help us Bring The M*utha F*cking R*ckus!

EventName: Rockburn Cross -- Event #5 of the 2026 BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series
EventNotes:
Venue and Course: 

Rockburn Cross is located within Rockburn Branch Park; a multi-use facility situated conveniently off I-95 in the Baltimore/Washington Corridor. There is a playground adjacent to the main course and the Li'l Belgian's course. Weather permitting, the Rockburn Skills Park  will be open and is a challenge for anyone but can also be an all-ages family activity. There will be a beer garden with offerings from Jailbreak Brewing and 2 Bold Chefs will be on hand with delicious Mediterranean food. 
AFC strives to provide the best CX course in the Mid-Atlantic and those who have raced here would agree it's always a challenge! There are super-fast woods sections, power sections, some (but never enough!) downhill recovery, hills and multiple areas with sand/gravel. It's a course that suits everyone at least part of the time!

Registration, Entry Fees, & Licensing:  

All registration and payment for this event, including race day registration, will be conducted through BikeReg.  Additional entries are offered at $20 ($25 on race day) when purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart.  If the entries are purchased separately during the pre-registration period, contact us for a partial refund; on event day a coupon code will be made available at the day-of registration table to achieve the same discounted price.  Entry fees will increase to $50 for adults and $25 for Junior Men & Women for race day registration, to reflect the day-of surcharge.  There will be no in-person sales at the event -- register online, either at home before coming out or on your phone at the event.  You MUST present your racing license (if you have one) or 1-Day receipt in order to be issued a bib, and you should also be prepared to show your confirmation email.  In order to expedite your entry, make sure you have completed the online waiver before approaching the day-of registration table.

Once pre-registered riders have been assigned bibs, this page will re-open for late/day-of registration in the early afternoon of Friday, 11/13/2026, and will remain open through event day; event day check-in will open by 7:30 AM.  Check-in and registration for all races will close 15 minutes prior to the scheduled start of the race.  There will be no exceptions made to this rule -- plan to show up timely for the race you want to enter.

A USA Cycling racing license is required for entry.  Riders who do not provide a USAC Annual racing license # at registration will be assessed an additional $15 for a Beginner 1-Day license.  This license is valid for entry only in fields that are open to Novice Men, Women, or Non-Binary riders.  For all other fields, you must present proof of an active USAC racing license (or a printed Authorization to Ride) showing your Cyclocross category and Racing Age.

Staging & Call Ups: 

Riders shall be staged in order of their assigned bib number.  Rockburn Cross is the fifth race of the 2026 BikeReg Cyclocross SuperSeries; therefore in fields eligible for SuperSeries points, bibs will be assigned to the first 8 riders (i.e., the front row) in order of their position in the Super Series standings on CrossResults.com ( https://www.crossresults.com/superseries ); remaining riders will be assigned bibs in order of the riders’ CrossResults.com ranking points; any remaining unranked riders will be assigned bibs by registration date & time.  For the Novice Men & Cat. 4/Novice Women, riders will be assigned bibs by registration date & time.  For all race categories, the first 4 positions in the third row are optionally available to the Race Director for discretionary call-ups.  Race day entries will be assigned remaining bib numbers on a first come, first served basis; riders registering after the close of pre-registration or on race day are not entitled to special treatment based on their position in the SuperSeries points standings or their CrossResults.com ranking.

BikeReg Cyclocross SuperSeries Rules:  

Rockburn Cross is a BikeReg Cyclocross SuperSeries event.  The event will is held under USA Cycling permit #16391.  USAC Cyclocross rules apply. The event will be held rain or shine. Podiums will be presented as soon as possible after each event.  Please remain near the podiums following your race if you place.  The protest period start will be announced and will last for 15 minutes. Mountain bikes are permitted, but bar-ends are not.

EventNotes:
WELCOME TO THE SOMERSET GRAVEL EPIC

presented by POPS Bike Shop and Team Somerset

Enjoy a fall cycling adventure through some of New Jersey’s most scenic gravel backroads and rail trails. Complimentary café and cider mill stops, pre- and post-ride refreshments and scenic routes featuring Ken Lockwood Gorge, Bedminster and Oldwick Gravel Roads, Columbia Trail and more. It's all here.  

Optional Pace Groups with Ride Leaders! Want to sit in and avoid the navigation?  Grab a wheel and enjoy good company.  Our ride leaders know the route, will keep your group together and make sure everyone hits the cafe with a smile.

All Bikes Welcome! Non-technical gravel roads and rail-trails… perfect for 35mm+ tires, though 40mm+ might up your fun factor.. Gravel, mountain, hybrid, fat tire, endurance, road bikes… you name it. Anything with decent tire clearance.

Oh, and “This is not a race.” We host a lot of races, so we thought we should point that out.

Registration

  • Online Registration Closes: Friday, November 13 at midnight. Day-Of Registration: $15 price increase applies.

  • Team Somerset Members: Save big on registration! Not a member yet? Join here for $40 and we'll extend your membership for all of 2027.

Schedule & Info

  • Location: Pops Bike Shop, 34 East Main St, Somerville, NJ

  • Check in 8:00 AM: Coffee, bagels and number pickup. Basic pre-ride mechanical support by Pops.

  • Start 9:00 AM: Rolling start (please depart by 9:30 AM).

  • Pace Groups: Ride your own pace, or ride with our experienced ride leaders 

    • C Pace: ~12 mph avg

    • B Pace: ~14 mph avg

    • A Pace: 16–18 mph avg

    • Ride leaders will stop at rest stops, for mechanicals etc. and will attempt to hold the advertised pace.

  • Parking: Free street and public lot parking all day! (Parking Map).

  • Course Maps: RideWithGPS / Strava links will be emailed a couple of days prior.

  • Pizza after-party for everyone back at the shop!

  • Helmets Required, bells recommended. We ride on open public roads; follow all traffic laws. YIELD TO HORSES: Horses are a common site on the Columbia Trail and our local gravel roads alike. Slow down, ring your bell and pass slowly with plenty of space.

  • This is a rain or shine event. Registrations are non-refundable/non-deferrable. Only canceled if a State of Emergency is declared.

 

Choose Your Route

1. Cider Loop — A 39 mile / 2,500 ft Elevation Gain loop through the rolling hills and gravel roads of Bedminster and Chester. C Pace Group or Self-Paced. Free hot drink & snack stop at Hacklebarney Cider Mill.

2. Long Route — A 70 mile / 4,800 ft Elevation Gain loop that adds iconic Oldwick gravel segments, Ken Lockwood Gorge, the Columbia Trail and more. Ride leaders at A Pace, B Pace, or Self-Paced. 2 free mid-ride stops at a cafe and the cider mill.

  • Note: Brief hike-a-bike sections may occur if storm damage is present in Ken Lockwood Gorge.

Photos Courtesy of Strava.

Ten years of Tour de Fall Line! - Join rvaMORE for a single track trail journey through the length of the James River’s fall line.

Experience a tour of the trails of the James River Basin by mountain bike, hosted by rvaMORE to raise money for to support the Richmond region's trail network.  All proceeds directly benefit rvaMORE to help enhance your outdoor experience on our local trails. Come out and explore with your fellow cycling enthusiasts.

Mountain Bike Routes:

Here is your chance to ride a route that hits all the major trail systems in the City of Richmond in one 52 mile loop! You will ride trails in a number of Richmond’s Parks, including the James River Park System, Forest Hill, Ancarrow’s, Dogwood Dell, Powhite, Pony Pasture and Larus. Shorter ride options of roughly 30 and 19 miles are available as well. All routes showcase what makes Richmond trails so unique and fun to ride - but be aware: these trails are all multi user and will be open to the public. Standard trail courtesy rules apply to all users on the day-of.

Mountain bikes are recommended with tires at least 2" wide as the courses will have plenty of dirt and lots of technical and challenging singletrack.  You will follow an unmarked course with aid stations along the way.  registered riders will have exclusive access to this year's routes through the Ride with GPS app, with a link in the pre-event email that goes out to all riders no later than Saturday November 14th morning.

You will be able to download a course file directly from Ride with GPS for use on your cycling GPS navigation device, or use the Ride with GPS mobile app to run navigation from your smartphone. While this should be FREE for you, it is wise to familiarize yourself with the app in advance so you aren't left navigating something new on event day.

Your registration includes a post-ride beverage and a meal: Lee's is back for another incredible year of chicken tenders and sides. For our vegetarian and vegan friends, we will have dairy/meat free pizza. Please make sure to select your meal preference during registration.

For our youth riders: we are excited to host a huge day adventure for you, with the ability to try to ride any of the mileages. Your registration must include the name of the registered parent or guardian riding with each youth member, in case of unlikely emergencies.

 Food will be available until 4pm, when the event closes. Plan to arrive at the finish area well before 4pm to ensure that you get your meal - we will begin packing up the day at 4pm sharp!

Please don't forget your smartphone, helmet, tubes, and other bike repair items you might need along the way. 
*Riders must bring their ID to check in at registration!*

Please note you will be riding on an open course, in an urban environment on a mix of singletrack and linked with on road connections. Most roads will be low traffic but the course does require short sections of some roads with vehicle traffic on them. 

Explore the course maps on RideWithGPS:  https://ridewithgps.com/events/505387-tour-de-fall-line-ten

Event Schedule:

52 Miler:  Day of Registration and Packet Pickup begins at 7AM.   Ride starts at 8:30 

30 Miler:  Day of Registration and Packet Pickup begins at 8AM.   Ride starts at 9:30 

19 Miler:  Day of Registration and Packet Pickup begins at 9AM.  Ride starts at 11:30

 

 Your registration to the tour includes:

•Snacks and drinks at all aid stations

•Post-ride party with a beverage and a meal.  Food until 4pm. 

• Exclusive access to the event routes on Ride with GPS

• Basic bike assistance at aid stations (free lube, tire pumping, etc.)

• And don’t forget, proceeds from your registration “fee” go back to support the trails you are riding!

 

Sponsored and supported by:

We have been putting on this event at Centennial Park in Lawrence, KS for over a decade.

Centennial Park is a spectator friendly venue in Central Larwence. Even though we have put on this race for more than a decade, the course has never been the same and we plan for a new and challenging course this year. In fact, our challenge is not to make the course too hard and with enough sections of recovery. There will be plenty of elevation change to push your limits!

EventNotes:
We are so excited for your child to participate in NICA Discovery! 

 

All NICA Discovery adult leaders are background checked and hold a coaching license from NICA.  There will always be at least 2 leaders who have current first aid training. 

 

New Friends is the introductory level and is aimed at children who are new to biking but have some limited experience with neighborhood or urban riding.  These are children who can already balance and pedal a bike, but may have never ventured “off road.” Games and activities work on learning to better ride and operate a bike preparation for later buildable skills, and increasing stamina. 

 

Participants must be able to ride a bike without training wheels before joining a program and must be 7 years of age by program start date.

 

NICA Discovery Little Rock meets at Camp Robinson and Two Rivers Bike Park on Tuesday evenings 5:00-6:30

October 13

October 20

October 27

November 3

November 10

November 17

 

Required Documentation

ONLINE: 

  • Registration for NICA Discovery is through the platform BikeReg.  Go to bikereg.com and search “NICA Discovery” to find your location. 

IN PERSON: 

  • Parents must print, review this CODE OF CONDUCT with their child, sing and bring it to the first session for their child to participate.  
  • Every rider is also required to have a waiver and medical release form signed on file with NICA.  A link to the waiver may be found HERE.  Parents are asked to show confirmation that the online waiver has been signed before their child participates.

Required Equipment

  • Helmet - Helmets should be less than 5 years old and fit your child’s head well without moving around while they ride. 
  • Footwear - Closed-toe (non-Croc like) shoes that fastened by laces, straps or buckles
  • Bike - Bike with knobby tires, gears, and two hand brakes. Bike tires should be no smaller than 20 inches.
  • Bike repair items - A replacement tube that fits your child’s tire. (dropped off at day one check in and returned at close of program if they are un-used.
  • Snug fitting small backpack  - Kids need to be able to carry water and snacks with them at all times.
  • Snacks/Hydration - Kids should always bring a snack and hydration with them to Discovery. 
    • Examples could include a granola bar, fruit snacks, or something that can easily be stored in a pocket or pack.
    • Hydration should consist of non caffeinated sports drinks or just good ole water! 

Recommended Equipment

  • Gloves - full-finger gloves to protect hands from abrasions in the case of a fall
  • Eye protection - generic sports glasses to protect from dust and debris (and bugs) kicked up while riding
  • Windbreaker /rain jacket/coat - weather conditions change throughout the season, your child should be prepared to ride in the conditions that are present on the day. Sessions will be altered or canceled if the weather conditions are unsafe. 
  • Athletic /Cycling pants- Loose fitting athletic pants. Cycling specific shorts are not required but some kids may be more comfortable.

What to Expect

Each session is broken down into 3 sections.  

  • Opener activities and objective/expectation setting
  • Skills activities and Games 
  • Wrap up and Reflection

There will be a  break mid-session for snacking/hydrating and general check in.

Each session builds on skills learned in the previous session.  To get the MOST out of NICA Discovery make sure your child can attend every session! 

For New Friends, the sessions consist of riding and playing in a park-like setting and are not trail dependent. Students will ride within that open space rather than out on trails, staying close to restroom facilities and support. 

 

Kids should come ready to learn, play, ride and explore!

Backpack examples 

A small pack that fits snugly and is just big enough to carry a water bottle and snacks, and maybe a small found treasure or two is great.

Helmet examples

Bike examples 

Guide to Kids' Bike Sizing

How to determine if the bike is the correct size

Standover:

While straddling the bike with feet flat on the ground, the rider should have about 2 inches of clearance between the top tube and their inseam.

The Donderdag! Youth Cyclocross Clinics are open to any youth rider eager to build confidence, make friends, and experience the excitement of cyclocross!

Our mission is to provide a safe, supportive, and fun environment where kids can develop fundamental bike handling skills, practice bike safety, and enjoy the outdoors with good food and great community. While we introduce clear, simple skills to help those interested in racing, our primary goal is helping every rider grow their strength, agility, and self-belief on two wheels. We encourage participants to show up ready to learn, support their peers, and simply give their personal best each week.

Driven by dedicated volunteers, Donderdag! fosters community leadership and mentorship. Teen riders are coached to guide and protect younger participants, while local volunteers help build a welcoming, inclusive cycling culture. Through our core coaching framework—Balance, Agility, Strength, and Exposure (B.A.S.E.)—riders gain lifelong skills that bring both confidence on the trail and success on race day.

Ultimately, Donderdag! exists to remind our community of the grace, connection, and strength found in grassroots coaching, leadership, and serving others.

EventNotes:
MT. NEBO ENDURO | NOVEMBER 21-22, 2026

We’re excited to return to the stunning Mount Nebo State Park! The Mt. Nebo Enduro is a mix of technical and flowy singletrack with stages for all levels. Perched high above the Arkansas River Valley, Mount Nebo offers amazing views.

Registration opens Friday, June 12th at 8am with participation based on a first-come, first-served basis. To create a rewarding enduro race experience, organizers reserve the right to limit overall event participation. Each participant’s entry includes:

  • One-day competition with up to 4-7 stages and 10-20 total miles of rider-designed racing with dedicated pre-race practice times the day prior to the race.
  • Sufficiently marked courses with maps emailed to participants the week of the event.
  • Lively mid-race aid stations with access to professional neutral mechanics and medical support.
  • Professional event timing with accuracy to the 1000th of a second and instant results.
  • Complimentary post-race meal and cold beverages (21+ for adult beverages, ID required) in a family-friendly festival setting.
  • Awards ceremony by category with prizes awarded 5 deep.

RACE VENUE

Mount Nebo is a prominent, flat-topped mountain mesa located in west-central Arkansas near Dardanelle. Rising 1,762 feet above sea level and soaring 1,350 feet directly out of the surrounding Arkansas River Valley, it is entirely enclosed by Mount Nebo State Park. Established in 1927, it serves as Arkansas's second-oldest state park and is a premier hub for outdoor recreation. 

Venue Address: 16728 West State Hwy. 155, Dardanelle, AR 72834

 

EVENT SCHEDULE

Final event schedule with packet pickup, official pre-ride, and start times will be released the week of the event. Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine except under extreme circumstances. When permittable, an official pre-ride/practice will be scheduled the day prior to Race Day(s). The Race Director reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances.

Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine except under extreme circumstances. When possible, an official practice will be scheduled the day prior to Race Day(s). The Race Director reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances. 

 

DRY CAMPING - To book your campsite, visit the Arkansas State Parks reservation page. 

SAFETY - This is not the time to skimp on protective equipment. Helmets are required to be worn on course during official event times and we highly suggest a full-face helmet, knee pads, and elbow pads.

TEMPERATURE - In November, Mount Nebo, Arkansas experiences cool, crisp weather. Temperatures typically reach an average high in the mid-50s (50°F to 54°F) and drop to average nightly lows in the low-to-mid 30s (30°F to 35°F).

WATER & SNACKS - While hydration will be available at select locations on course, riders are encouraged to plan to carry at least 50-60 ounces of water and enough snacks to sustain themselves under strenuous exercise.

Every year an event comes along that tests mental and physical strengths of its racers like no other. Pisgah Productions proudly presents the hardest (and most fun) thing you will do this year….. the DOUBLE DARE.

Teams of two riders will race to reach up to 10 checkpoints (CPs) per day, two days in a row. The race begins at 10AM on Saturday and every team must be back before 10PM. SINGLE-DARE! The one-day category at Double-Dare!!! Teams of two riders will race up to 10 checkpoints, in any order, and return to the start/finish the fastest. Checkpoint locations will remain secret until start time and there is no suggested route. Start time for the one-day category will be 10AM Saturday and Final cutoff will be 10PM.

For both DOUBLE-DARE and SINGLE-DARE:

There will be nothing at the checkpoints other than pre-existing landmarks. Every team must carry a reliable digital camera to photograph the landmarks as proof of being there.

Can you believe it’s our eighteenth year! Join us for Turkey Bike on  Saturday November 21st. If you haven't done Turkey Bike before here's how it works. Riders meet at Cycle Craft in Parsippany and roll out at 9:00 and head to King’s supermarket in Boonton to buy a bunch of turkeys. Then, we ride over to Smartworld Coffee in Denville where the Community Food Bank of New Jersey is there to receive the birds. The ride is fairly easy and you only have to carry your turkey for a few miles. We recommend using a sturdy back pack or pannier bags on a rack to carry your bird. String bags are not any fun to use and front baskets can be tricky to manage with a 20lb turkey in it. There is no entry fee so your only cost is the cost of the turkey that you pick out.

When you arrive at Smartworld we'll treat to you hot beverages and delicious snacks as our way of saying "thanks!" for participating. Riders then head back to Cycle Craft. It's a fun way to do something good!

Riders meet at Cycle Craft Parsippany with check in beginning at 8:00AM and the ride rolls at 9:00AM. If you have any questions please email brendan@cyclecraft.com

Go Nuts Regionals (GNR) eMTB Rules as follows: 
1) Maximum 750watts - assistance up to 20 miles per hour - Pedaling assistance only. No hand or foot throttle allowed. Automatic disqualification. Bicycles must remain locked, i.e., no modification of wheel sensor from factory circumference or any other modification to manipulate the factory set speed of the bike.
2) Throttle mechanisms are prohibited.
3) Studded tires are prohibited.
4) It is forbidden to change e-bike during the event even if the rider finishes the event with the same race plate.
5) It is forbidden to recharge the e-bike or battery in the technical zone during the GNR event.
6) Technical assistance consists of the replacement or repairs of any part of the e-bike at the exception of the frame, wheels or battery.
7) Riders age categories are 18 and under, 19-39, 40-49 and 50 plus for Classes; Amateurs, Experts and Open Pro. 
8) Riders can only use the battery in place on their bike and cannot carry or switch out an additional battery during the competition.
9) Race course length will be 4.5 - 7 miles depending on difficulty. Steeper climbs and more technical than normal XC will be tested on some courses. Each category will start an hour apart and should be completed within their hour.
10) Races will be conducted regardless of weather conditions.  In the event of rain or other unfavorable conditions, it may be necessary to alter the order of the event schedule, including but not limited to, adjusting the length of the race or delaying or stopping the program completely.  Should a delay occur, every effort will be made to resume the schedule in a timely fashion if conditions significantly improve.
11) No headphones, earphones or sound devices permitted. Horns and bells are permitted.
12) Riders are required to wear the appropriate helmet. Other protective gear is optional; gloves, goggles, elbow/knee guards, etc.
13) Shirt, shoes, and pants/shorts required. Clipless or flat pedals are both permitted.
15) An E-Mountain Bike is a bike operated with two energy sources, human pedal power and an electric engine, which only provides assistance when the rider is pedaling.
16) The course will the taped and marked. Any rider cutting the course will be disqualified.
17) Any behavior deemed in appropriate or unsportsmanlike like conduct will not be tolerated. Verbal or physical infractions will result in a disqualification.

Severe weather policy
Unless otherwise posted, race will be held. Safety of all racers is our main priority. If there is a delay or cancellation due to weather conditions, racers are responsible for checking information posted by director.
The information will be posted on the homepage of website, social network avenues, and via email up to 72 hours prior to the race.

Transfer/Refund Policy
There will be no registration refunds once registration is processed. We will allow transfers to upcoming races. All transfers must be requested 10 days prior and is only allowed for races that were rescheduled. Transfers will not be allowed 10 days before race or after race.

EventNotes:
Boy howdy, it's Fall Fuckaround time again! Once again we're riding to benefit The Lancaster Conservancy and The Marietta Woods Project. We spend a lot of time enjoying these lands and we wanna chip in. 

 

Morning of:

We'll be starting at the shop, 414 N. Mary Street, Lancaster. There is plenty of free street parking in every direction around the shop. If it's raining and you need a dry staging area, there is a reasonably priced parking garage just a few blocks away at 220 N. Water Street, Lancaster. Our friends at Endo Cafe will have the coffee trailer there to keep you warm and caffeinated before we shove off.  West Art will be open at 7am with coffee and pastries just a few blocks up Lemon Street.  If you're looking for a full breakfast, Prince Street Cafe will be open at 7am and Lancaster's Central Market will be open at 6am. If you've never been, Central Market is the social hub of Lancaster and is worth getting up a little early to see. Whatever you do, be at the shop by 9:30 and be ready to roll at 10:00. 

 

The ride:

There are two courses, however both courses also have an alternate route for folks with road bikes (and road bike shoes.) All courses are linked below. There are no course markings, please download the course to a computer or use Ride With GPS. You will have phone reception the entire day, so if things get fucky, just find your way home using your phone. 

The long course has a substantial (3/4 mile?) hike-a-bike section, non-road shoes are highly recommended. Both courses follow the length of Suzy's Hole, which is light singletrack with a couple very easy creek crossings. The only aid station on the day is immediately after the Suzy's/Trolley Road trail section. Mom and Dad von Fancypants will be serving up the treats. 

After the aid station there's a short section of chunky railroad ballast, then a bunch of miles of some of the most beautiful rail trail anywhere. While on the rail trail, riders will cross the Safe Harbor bridge, which provides expansive views of the Susquehanna River. After leaving the rail trail, you'll wind through Millersville and back to the  shop. 

 

Long Course: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/38049384

Long Course (Road): https://ridewithgps.com/routes/41451896

Short Course: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/41098048

Short Course (Road): https://ridewithgps.com/routes/41451829

 

The Dirtbag After-Party:

We'll have fire pits to stand around. Cabalar will be open with the meats and the non-meats (OMG SRSLY the falafel burger is a revelation). Lancaster celebrity Drew Bell will be there to regale us with stories over the fire pits and serve us Endo Tunies (sorry hornballs, he's married). Lancaster's vegan comfort food spot, Bad Garden Kitchen, will be open just a few blocks away. The Pennsylvania Dirtbags will be there too- we have no idea what they have planned, and for liability's sake, we don't want to know. 

 

The Big Dumb Awards Show and Raffle:

Back for 2025: The Bill & Ted Awards for Excellence in the field of Being Excellent. The trophies are recycled. The awards have no value. But GOSH DARNIT the sentiment is real. Last year, for the third consecutive year, the Yinzer contingent went home with the most hardware (but no police citation). Past awards have included: The Sarah Woshe Award for General Gangstery, The Leo Quisimbing Spirit of Gravel Award, The Scotty Clark “Clean Drawers” Award, Least Improved, Best Dressed, Worst Bike, Worst Dressed, Best Bike, The Linette Award for Best Colors, and Least Offensive Odor. Also back for 2026 is the Highest Finisher award, although the homies from Action Wheels are always hard to beat here. (One year they finished so high that they left the trophy on the roof of their team car and drove off with it up there, never to be seen again.) Other awards categories will be decided on the fly. All of them will be stupid.  

This year's raffle will be bigger and a little less of a clusterfuck. Raffles will be announced every half hour starting at 3:00. Winners must be present, but raffles will be going off every 30 minutes for the duration of the evening. The big stuff will be raffled after the awards ceremony.

 

Please don't take any of it too seriously.

EventName: The Ride Series MTB Skills Clinics: DROP PROGRESSION & JUMP PROGRESSION NOV 27TH
EventNotes:
The Ride Series is different. Your expectations should be high as you enter the hospitality of our classroom setting. A comfortable Kijaro chair awaits your presence and the cover our 10x20 tents provides reprieve from the elements. Prepare yourself to be immersed in an environment that provides the perfect opportunity for you to be open to embracing and practicing the proper technique. Instant feedback from our coaching staff will have you progressing like never before! Are YOU ready??

DROP PROGRESSION: Ground School and SP Skills Park 

Welcome to a world where Physics, Gravity, and the engineering of your bike are embraced to help guide you off drops like never before. It's not rocket science, it's rational thought manifesting in you being more confident and landing drops with more stability than you ever thought possible. 

JUMP PROGRESSION Session: Ground School and All American Heroes Jumpline

This event is all about getting comfortable in the air. That starts with a solid understanding of what it takes to get into the air properly. It's also critical to get as MANY reps as possible in a controlled environment and that's what the TRS ground school setting gives you.

Our Pro level coaches break down the dynamics involved with jumping a bike. Based on over 70 years experience, they guide you through their real world experience and give you key insight and cues on what to do and also what not to do. 

After showcasing the proper technique, you'll work through a series of reps and the distance will incrementally increase as your comfort level increases. Analysis and feedback using slow motion video will have you "busting big" in no time.

There's no substitute for experience when it comes to jumping a bike. The only problem is that experience in the right setting can be hard to come by. You'll get tons reps on our jump lines and receive valuable feedback in the moment.
RIDERS MUST HAVE:
- Experience jumping
- Full suspension bikes with suspension in working order
- Full safety gear including pads (Full Face helmet not required, but suggested)

This class is intended for riders with jump experience and will move at a specified pace. Coaching staff reserves the right to hold riders to pre determined distances based on performance.

Please reach out if you are unsure if this class is a proper fit for you.

EventNotes:
Please read this!
 

Welcome to our FREE monthly ride! Ride start times vary by season to give us the best trail conditions and safest experience—May through September we roll out at 8:00 AM CT, and October through April we begin at 2:00 PM CT. We meet at the lower parking lot at Turkey Mountain Urban Wilderness Park, 6800 S Elwood Ave, Tulsa, OK 74132. Restrooms are available.

 

We will have ride leaders for skill levels between Beginner to Advanced. If you're new to mountain biking, OR have never taken WeROK’s Fundamentals, or other formal fundamentals skills clinics (even if you have been riding some), we REQUIRE YOU to start with the WeROK Fundamental Skills Session during registration. Regardless of your riding experience we feel taking this skills session will help improve your riding and create a better riding experience for all.

 

Loaner Bikes: Please refer to your registration confirmation letter. 
 

Cancellation/Bad Weather Policy: If bad weather develops we aim to cancel the event by 6:00 am the day of the ride.  Stay tuned to social media for announcements. We also follow Trailbot, in case Turkey Mountain trails are “closed” or “delayed”.  We do not have “rain dates”. 

 

Choosing appropriate group: First choose your riding and fitness level, then choose the best description among the groups. Once a group fills, the waitlist option will open. If you have a friend with the same skill level with whom you want to ride, help us out by registering together ASAP, in the same ride level, AND in same group number. Other than cancellations, we CANNOT GUARANTEE we can make any changes to groups, especially at the last minute, since we have group size restrictions. This delivers the best possible ride experience for all! If you don't end up riding with your friends, don't worry, you'll have the opportunity to make new ones!
 

Not sure which group to join? Ride levels are based on YOUR CURRENT skill and endurance levels. We want everyone to have the best and safest experience possible so we use a “rating” system to help align you with the right ride group. Please review the skills, endurance, mileage and proposed trails. Being in the right group makes a better, safer ride for all. If you are still unsure about which group might be for you just contact us at ride@werok.org. P.S. It is perfectly fine to “repeat” a level! Mastery of ALL levels takes time and practice. Please don’t rush yourself, nor succumb to peer pressure. NOTE: WeROK’s skill level names and colors are relative to Turkey Mountain trails. Other trail systems’ color designations could mean their Blue is (y)our Black, so be wise!
 

Advancing to next groups: A great way to know if you are ready to progress to the next ride level is if (1) you felt comfortable with skills necessary at your current level, and (2) you were able to keep up with the ride leader the entire ride and felt like you could have ridden longer. 

 

GROUP CHOICES:
 

1. FUNDAMENTAL SKILLS SESSION 

Select this group if you have never ridden a mountain bike, it’s been longer than you’d like to admit, OR you've never taken any type of basic mtb skills lessons before. Welcome! You have to start somewhere and this is the place! Even the most advanced riders should brush up on these essentials, and certainly, if you feel rusty, this session will help you. This session will cover the fundamentals of mountain biking, and then you'll hit the trail for a 2-3 mile ride. Successful completion of WeROK’s Fundamentals (or its equivalent) is required for advancement to next groups. Departure from this policy requires approval by a WeROK ride leader.

  • Skill Level: Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals are required (we may have loaner pedals available; email us ahead of time at ride@werok.org).
  • Skills you can perform: no requirement, you will definitely learn a skill or two after this session. 
  • Fitness Level: No requirement other than participate in possible heat for up to 2 hours.
  • Example of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, no rocks; double track near Bomb Cellar; the grassy fields; the Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop. 

2. FUNDAMENTALS TO GREEN Group

Select this group if you have taken the Fundamental Skills session, you feel more confident with those skills, and you are looking for a very easy-going transition to green trails. You will have a skills refresher for up to 15 minutes.

  • Skill Level: Confident Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals strongly encouraged (see above re: loaner pedals).
  • Skills you can perform: Staying upright while pedaling, skills learned in Fundamentals Group are beginning to make sense, and your confidence is growing.
  • Fitness Level: Completed a Fundamentals session with minimal fatigue
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with occasional flat, mellow rocks or roots, no significant downhill or uphill; Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop; the very first section of LoChi Connector.
  • Duration: 3-5 miles, maybe longer in cooler weather, no longer than 1.5 hours after refresher portion

3. GREEN Group
You’ve ridden on the dirt trails multiple times by now, and you’re getting the hang of things. You’re mastering the Fundamentals Skills, and your bike operating and handling skills feel smoother. No Fundamentals refresher portion provided.

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: Level pedals while coasting; one finger braking; becoming more comfortable with neutral and ready positions; and smoother corners/berms.
  • Fitness level: Able to ride steady at a comfortable pace for 30 minutes on easy terrain, and may need a breather while climbing, or at the top.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with a variety of low, smooth surface changes; more variety of up and downhill; LoChi; UHF or All Up with rests.
  • Duration: 5-7 miles,1.5 to 2.0 hours 

4. OPEN Group

Looking for new challenges! You are ready to explore more trail features (obstacles) and a variety of up and downhills, with limited stops. Mileage varies. No Fundamentals refresher provided. 

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus-to-Intermediate.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: GREEN skills are solid, but you’re out of saddle more instinctively with level pedals; in and out of neutral/ready position more smoothly; frequent appropriate shifting; smoother, smoother berms and corners; want to ride across straight bridges and skinnies 3-5 feet wide; comfortable choosing lines through rockier terrain, or between tight trees.
  • Fitness level: You’re riding a few times a week. Can ride a WeROK course continuously unless learning steep or more technical terrain. Pushing the pace uphill.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, more roots and rocks, twists and turns. The small bridge on OLD Lo Chi, All Up, UHF, Stay Gold Loop, Naharkey clockwise, maybe counterclockwise. Sessioning features within your skill set, such as the small skinny on Family Loop.
  • Duration: 8-10 miles, 2 hours with some stopping.

EventName: Tacchino Ciclocross -- Event #7 of the 2026 BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series
EventNotes:
The Venue:  we have an exciting venue -- the Montgomery County Agricultural History Farm Park, which provides us with lots of terrain and options for fun and challenging cyclocross features.

Parking:  parking will be adjacent to the course. Look for signs at the entrance.

Alcohol Prohibited!  The venue is a Montgomery County park.  Park regulations prohibit alcohol. Please do not jeopardize our use of the park.

Food Trucks:   There will be at least one food truck and we are working on more. 

Medical/First Aid:  There will be EMT support on-site.  First aid will be available at the registration shelter. 

The Event:  Tacchino Ciclocross is a BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series event.  The event is held under USA Cycling permit #16399.  All USAC Cyclocross rules apply. Event will be held rain or shine.  Prizes will be awarded as soon as possible after each event.  Please remain near the podiums following your race if you place.  The start of the protest period will be announced. 

Course Description:  The course will be classic Mid-Atlantic.  There are rolling hills, a challenging section through the woods, numerous off-cambers, gravel paths, and at least one set of obstacles.  There will be one double-sided pit on the course.

****PROFESSIONAL CHIP TIMING by Insight Timing Services****

Registration, Entry Fees, & Licensing:  all registration and payment for this event, including race day registration, will be conducted through BikeReg.  Addtional entries are offered at $20 ($25 on race day) when purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart.  If the entries are purchased separately during the pre-registration period, contact us for a partial refund; on event day a coupon code will be made available at the day-of registration table to achieve the same discounted price.  Entry fees will increase to $50 for adults and $25 for Juniors for race day registration, to reflect the day-of surcharge.  There will be no in-person sales at the event -- register online, either at home before coming out or on your phone at the event.  You MUST present your racing license (if you have one) or 1-Day receipt in order to be issued a bib, and you should also be prepared to show your confirmation email.  In order to expedite your entry, make sure you have completed the online waiver before approaching the day-of registration table. 

This page will re-open for late/day-of registration in the afternoon of the Friday prior to the event.  Race day registration and check-in will open by 7:30 AM.  Check-in and registration for all races will close 20 minutes prior to the scheduled start of the race.  There will be no exceptions made to this rule -- plan to show up timely for the race you want to enter.

A USA Cycling racing license is required for entry.  Riders who do not provide a USAC Annual racing license # at registration will be assessed an additional $15 for a Beginner 1-Day license.  This license is valid for entry only in fields that are open to Novice Men, Women, or Non-Binary riders.  For all other fields, you must present proof of an active USAC racing license showing your Cyclocross category and Racing Age.

Any current National Cyclocross Champions shall be granted free entry, but must wear their national jersey in the class in which it was won.

Series Points:  SuperSeries points are awarded for all races EXCEPT the Novice Men and Cat. 4/Novice Women races.

On-Course Warmup:  riders shall only enter the course for warmup laps between races in the designated area near the starting grid.  The gate will be the only entry point to the course and entry time will be designated by the race officials.

Staging:  riders shall be staged in order of their assigned bib number.  Tacchino CX is the 7th event of the 2026 BikeReg Cyclocross SuperSeries.  In fields eligible for SuperSeries points, bibs will be assigned to the first 8 riders (i.e., the front row) in order of their position in the Super Series standings on CrossResults.com ( https://www.crossresults.com/superseries ); remaining riders will be assigned bibs in order of the riders’ CrossResults.com ranking points; any remaining unranked riders will be assigned bibs by registration date & time.  For the Novice Men & Cat. 4/Novice Women, riders will be assigned bibs by registration date & time.  For all race categories, the first 4 positions in the third row are optionally available to the Race Director for discretionary call-ups.  Race day entries will be assigned remaining bib numbers on a first come, first served basis; riders registering on race day are not entitled to special treatment based on their position in the SuperSeries points standings or their CrossResults.com ranking.

Staging Procedure:  riders will fill the starting grid by bib number, 8 riders at a time, as specified in the USA Cycling Cyclocross rulebook when so directed by the officials; the officials will fill any gaps left by DNS or late-arriving riders as appropriate.  ALL RIDERS MUST ASSEMBLE IN THE PRE-STAGING CHUTE NO LATER THAN 10 MINUTES BEFORE THEIR START!   Riders arriving late to staging may be staged at the back of the starting grid at discretion of the Chief Referee.

MABRA Mission Statement:

“To promote the sport of bicycle racing in the Mid-Atlantic region, principally within the states of Delaware and Maryland, the northern portion of the state of Virginia, the eastern panhandle of West Virginia, and the District of Columbia;

To foster camaraderie and fellowship among culturally, racially and gender diverse bicycle racers and enthusiasts within the Mid-Atlantic;

To help ensure bicycle racers and enthusiasts in the Mid-Atlantic have an equal opportunity to participate in bicycle racing and activity without discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, age, gender, sexual orientation, or national origin;

To support and facilitate the efforts of its members, clubs, and other organizations that promote diverse, inclusive and equitable bicycle racing/activity/engagement in the Mid-Atlantic;

To support the efforts of its members in promoting bicycle racing and events for local, regional, national and international competition; and

To undertake such actions as are necessary, proper, desirable, advisable, or convenient for the furtherance and accomplishment of the foregoing purposes, provided that such actions do not exceed the bounds accepted for a District of Columbia nonprofit corporation.” 

* The 150 rider limit is for the combined field in a race.  Registration will close once the limit has been reached by any combination of classes within the field. 

* Classes designated “Masters” are open to Men and Women. Minimum Racing Age and categories quoted are for Men; minimum Racing Age and categories for Women per USAC rules.

** Promoter reserves the right to increase total prize purse as race day gets closer.

Gender Equality & Transgender Policy: 

Classes designated “Masters” are open to Men and Women. The minimum Racing Age and categories quoted are for Men; please see the current USAC Rulebook for minimum Racing Age and categories for Women.  The Super Series  welcomes everyone to participate in the gender category they feel is most appropriate to them, as described in USA Cycling policies: https://usacycling.org/about-us/governance/transgender-athletes-policy

The collective teams comprising the MABRA Super Series are committed to providing inclusive and equitable racing events.  The Super Series is proudly adding non-binary categories (1/2/3 and 4/5) to race during the women's races.  This addition is to honor all of our cyclists and provide a category that allows everyone to race with how they identify.  

In the event that USAC chooses to amend current policy to align with UCI changes for our transgender racers, then WTF (women-trans-femme) will be added to our non-binary categories as WTFNB.

Event contact information: 

www.squadracoppi.org 

https://www.facebook.com/squadracoppi  

Race Director:  Tom Faucette 202-360-6886

Thanks for reading, and see you on race day!

Calling all mountain bikers! It’s time to cap off your season with some adrenaline-pumping, late-season racing. 

Here's a great preview of some of the many fun sections of the Frosty Woods MTB course:

Why ride?
Shake off those post-Thanksgiving calories with a thrilling ride through the crisp, frosty woods of Ringwood State Park. The course is designed to challenge your skills while giving you the perfect mix of fun and competition.

Prime conditions, unbeatable vibes!
Late November riding in New Jersey? Absolutely! With the shifting weather patterns, early December now offers fantastic, fast conditions for mountain biking—cold enough to keep you cool, but not too icy to stop you from tearing up the trails.

Whether you're looking to set a personal record or simply enjoy one last race before the year ends, Frosty Woods MTB is where you want to be. Don’t miss your chance to ride, race, and celebrate the season in style!
