EventNotes:
Fall is the best time to ride bikes

  • CCAP School Clubs begin riding in September
  • Teams ride together in a supportive positive environment led by USA Cycling certified coaches
  • Riders learn to improve their skills and stamina along with bicycle and trail maintenance
  • Clubs practice twice a week
  • Two group ride adventure trips are scheduled:
    • Bluff Point in Groton, CT
    • Watrous Park in Cromwell, CT

A properly fitting bicycle helmet and mountain bike in good working condition are required.  This gear can be provided if your junior rider does not have currently have a helmet or bicycle.

All families joining a CCAP Program are required to adhere to CCAP Protocols.  These are found in the waivers section of the online registration form on BikeReg.  Please review and confirm with your signature.

WCC Membership 2026 

WestCoast Cycling Society (WCC) has been primarily a mountain bike club for many years, but with the reduction in XC racing and activity, we have transitioned into a road, gravel and Cyclocross focused group.  We still do mountain biking, but opportunities for racing are somewhat limited.
A previous requirement for membership with WCC was a Competition License or General Membership with Cycling BC (CBC).  Since 2025, this requirement has been dropped.  We no longer require a CBC membership or license to join WCC. There is no distinction between licensed and non-licensed members.
WCC is officially affiliated with CBC, the benefit of this is that we can put on races under the stewardship of CBC.  This requires that at least one member of WCC must hold a Competition and Technical License with CBC, a condition that we do indeed meet.

There is always support for anyone that wants to organize an event, a ride or an adventure that club members can participate in.  Some that come to mind …. weeknight Mt.  Seymour Road climbs, a mid summer Mt. Baker climb (followed by burgers or ice-cream), North Shore Mountain bike epics and local gravel escapades.

More General benefits for WCC membership. 
-  Opportunity to join and connect with members for recreational and racing opportunities
-  No charge (as in free) entry into any racing events organized and run by WCC.  Club members all chip in to help organize and run events as well as race (the primary objective).  Vanier Park CX is our primary event focus.
-  We have a great relationship with Schwalbe Tyres which results in us being able to order great tires to keep us all running rubber side down, all with a decent discount.   https://www.schwalbetires.com/
-  Blonyx Canada has been good enough to support our members with a 25% Discount on their nutrition and supplement products.  The discount code is sent out monthly and can be paired with they existing 15% subscription discount.  I can vouch for the electrolyte and the protein powder (NO Stevia …. yipee).    https://blonyx.ca/
-  While limited in scope, we also have a sponsorship arrangement with RaceFace Easton for discounts on parts and accessories.  Again, it helps with keeping our bikes running and up to date.      https://www.raceface.ca/

EventNotes:
Please visit the West Texas Showdown website for more information about this event and routes.  

West Texas Showdown

Terlingua, TX | Dec. 4th - 6th, 2026

The West Texas Showdown isn’t just a race — it’s a battle against the desert itself. Big Bend delivers jagged singletrack, endless horizons, and conditions as raw as they come. Wild, unpredictable, and unforgiving — this is where legends are made.

The third stage of the Texas Showdown Series and the crown jewel of the Texas Showdown Triple Crown.  Set in the Big Bend region of Texas, this event promises to test every ounce of grit, skill, and determination.

This is mountain desert country — wild, remote, and raw. The terrain is rugged, the weather unpredictable, and resources are scarce. Nearly everything in the desert either bites, pinches, stings, or grabs. Don’t be scared — but don’t come unprepared.

Big Bend – Home of the Showdown

Big Bend Ranch State Park and the surrounding desert country embody the spirit of West Texas: wide-open basins framed by volcanic cliffs, deep canyons carved by the Rio Grande, and horizons that shift with every mile.

It’s one of the most remote places in the lower 48, where solitude comes naturally and silence is as striking as the scenery. Out here, self-reliance isn’t optional — it’s survival. By day, the desert unfolds in stark beauty: ocotillo stretching skyward, hidden springs tucked into arroyos, and dirt roads that climb to vistas you’ll never forget. By night, you’ll ride under one of the darkest skies in North America, the Milky Way blazing overhead in a show few places on Earth can match.

Event Options

Showdown – 390 miles of Glory & Pain
This is the flagship route: long, raw, and unrelenting. It starts with a paved rollout from Terlingua before plunging straight into the wilds of Big Bend Ranch State Park. Riders will grind up gravel park roads, hike through rugged arroyos, and battle through stretches of singletrack where “rideable” depends on your skill, stamina, and stubbornness.

Highlights:

  • Marfa (Mile ~200): A quirky West Texas art town, home of the mysterious “Marfa Lights” and the famous Prada “storefront.” Will quite literally be a desert oasis for riders.
  • Pinto Canyon: One of the most dramatic landscapes in Texas. A twisting, jaw-dropping descent through volcanic cliffs. Sunrise or sunset here is unforgettable.
  • Rio Grande Stretch: Long paved miles along the border, with Mexico just across the river. Stunning views and a glimpse of life in the small border towns.
  • The Death Loop: A 50-mile finale north of Terlingua that will test what’s left of your legs and your willpower.

Stats: ~390 miles | 60% unpaved / 40% paved

Slowdown – 290 miles of Dust & Determination
A shorter, but still fierce route through Big Bend. The Slowdown trims the distance but keeps the character: gravel park roads, rough country tracks, stretches of arroyo riding, and just enough singletrack to keep you honest. This is a full-on bike expedition into one of the harshest and most beautiful places in the country.

Highlights:

  • Remote gravel stretches deep inside Big Bend Ranch SP
  • Rough, sandy arroyos that force you to wrestle with your bike as much as ride it
  • Expansive desert views that make every climb worth it
  • Just enough pavement to catch your breath before the dirt pulls you back in

Stats: ~290 miles | 48% unpaved / 52% paved

Lowdown – The Gateway to Big Bend
 The Lowdown is our non-competitive, guided bikepacking group ride. Designed to introduce riders to the magic of Big Bend in a slightly more approachable way. This route is not to be taken lightly, the distance is shorter, but the miles are hard. A good option for those with experience bikepacking, but want to try something more extreme.

Ride leaders and sweepers will help guide the way, but this is still a self-supported trip. You’ll need to carry your own food, water, and camping gear. Along the way you’ll experience the vastness, solitude, and starlit skies that make Big Bend unforgettable.

Highlights:

  • Long stretches of gravel roads and dry arroyos inside Big Bend Ranch SP
  • Nights spent under some of the darkest skies in North America
  • Bring your big tires and probably suspension

Stats: ~85 miles over 3 days | 80% unpaved / 20% paved

Schedule

Thursday, Dec. 3rd

  • 12–8pm: Rider check-in & tracker pickup
     
  • 8–9pm: Pre-race meeting at TBD

Friday, Dec. 4th

  • 7am: Showdown & Slowdown & Lowdown - Grand Departs

Saturday, Dec. 5th

  • All day: Ride Your Damn Bike

Sunday, Dec. 6th

  • All day: Celebrate finishers at Temple of the Bird
     
  • 5pm: Hoedown starts w/ live local music
     
  • 7–8pm: Awards + raffle
     
  • 10pm: Party winds down
     

Host City & HQ

Our host town is Terlingua, TX — a once-thriving mercury mining hub turned ghost town, now home to a small but eclectic community of artists, adventurers, and desert dreamers. Nestled between Big Bend Ranch State Park and Big Bend National Park, Terlingua’s ruins, shacks, and quirky dwellings create a setting unlike anywhere else.

Race HQ will be at the Temple of the Bird and it'll be our home for the weekend.

Getting Here

Terlingua is off the beaten path — there are no direct planes, trains, or buses. The nearest airports are in Midland or El Paso; from there, it’s a long desert drive. If you’re arriving via Alpine or Marfa, you’ll also pass through a Border Patrol checkpoint before reaching town.

Rider Notes

  • Bike Choice: This is MTB country — rocky climbs, rugged singletrack, arroyo crossings, and rough gravel. Leave your gravel bike at home.
  • Self-Supported: Riders must carry food, water, navigation, and repair gear. Resources are extremely limited.
  • Leave No Trace: The desert is fragile. Pack it in, pack it out. No catholing. Carry a waste bag.
  • Risks: Remote terrain, wildlife, weather extremes, and isolation. This is not an event for the faint of heart or the unprepared.
     

FAQ

Why don’t the routes go into Big Bend National Park?
Bikes are not allowed on singletrack trails inside the National Park. All riding is on roads only. Big Bend Ranch State Park offers far better opportunities for rugged, off-road adventure.  The National Park is also not open to these types of events…yet!

Will I pass through a Border Patrol checkpoint?
Yes. If you’re driving in from Alpine or Marfa, you will pass through a permanent Border Patrol checkpoint north of Terlingua. Have your ID handy.  You will also have a Border checkpoint if you are doing the Showdown or Slowdown heading into Marfa.  

What’s the weather like in December?
Riders should be prepared for temperatures ranging from below freezing overnight to warm, sun-filled afternoons. Weather in Big Bend Ranch State Park can change rapidly, and strong winds, cold rain, and freezing temperatures are all possible. Conditions may vary dramatically across the route due to changes in elevation, terrain, and exposure.

? What bike should I bring?
This is MTB terrain. Wide tires, suspension, and durable gear are highly recommended. Gravel bikes will not cut it here.

? How self-supported is this event?
Completely. Riders are expected to carry their own food, water, tools, and navigation. Resupply points are limited, so plan carefully. Rescue vehicles will be available to extract riders off course if needed, but when you're riding, you're on your own!

? How do I handle waste?
Big Bend’s desert ecosystem is delicate. Riders must follow Leave No Trace principles. That means packing out all trash and carrying a waste bag — no catholing allowed.

The legendary New England Cyclocross Finale Returns for its 19th year!
 

 

49% of extremely biased twitteratti agree:  this race is basically the World Championships


Hey, you probably noticed from the category names that this isn't a USAC sanctioned event.   If you can't figure out what field to register for, the answer is either "Beginner" or "Singlespeed."  Or you can always email us any questions using the "contact event" link above.  

 

What's with the name?:

It's a combination of this and that.


Who races when??  How do I win money? 

  • Jedi Men and Jedi 40+ Men will race together (1 start) with 40+ denoted in results.  Shared prize list of $500 with $100 bonus cash for 40+.

  • Jedi Women and Jedi 40+ Women will race together (1 start) with 40+ denoted in results.  Shared prize list of $500 with $100 bonus cash for 40+

  • Singlespeed men, fat bikes and women will race together (2 starts) with separate results and prizes.

  • Riders can race in additional races for $20.

  • Start positions determined by rider rankings at crossresults.com

  • Mountain Bikes allowed in any category.  Even if they have bar ends.  Unless the bar ends have pointy knives on them.

What's new this year?

We have a food truck (Thai Chili)!  

There's a bunch of new weird motocross lines and piles of dirt to play with!  We don't know exactly how we're going to use it all yet, but we do know it's gonna be good.

What's your inclusivity policy?

Ice Weasels is a celebration of cyclocross that everyone should feel welcome to be a part of.  Athletes are encouraged to show up and and race as their authentic selves in whatever category makes the most sense to them.

We have a zero tolerance policy for harassment so if anyone is being a jerk about anyone's identity (or anything else for that matter) let us know and we'll take care of it.
 


What's your refund policy?

We grant all refunds, all the time, for any reason.  Missing the race is punishment enough, we don't need to rub it in by keeping your money.  If you're on the fence, just register now (before your field is full!) and ask for a refund if you change your mind.

Welcome to the Pie Ride!

Keo, Arkansas • Saturday, December 5, 2026

Nestled in Southern Lonoke County (SoLoCo), Keo is a bike-friendly town of just 207 residents that knows how to roll out the welcome mat. We’re glad you’re here to ride, celebrate, and of course—eat pie!

Routes

  • SoLoCo 25

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/52192236

  • SoLoCo 35

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/52192137

Start Line

The ride begins at 10:00 AM sharp from the Keo Airstrip on Pecan Road. The airstrip is located just half a mile east of town at the intersection of Pecan Road and Cemetery Road.

Pre-Ride Happy Hour

  • When: Wednesday, December 2
  • Where: Moody Brews 414 E. 21st Street, Pettaway Square, Little Rock, AR.
  • Time: 4:00 PM – 7:00 PM

We are celebrating Happy Hour at Moody Brews and want to introduce you to a really cool partnership between the brewery, South Lonoke County (SoLoCo) and the Pie Ride! Moody Brews gets their rice for their New Ground Pils from Isbell Farms, located in SoLoCo. Brewer Josiah Moody then transforms that rice into New Ground Pils, a light lager, which will be served at the Pecan Festival. We are going green this year and only providing a bib number, safety pins and a drop bag to be used on ride day. Drop your street clothes at the start line and they will be at the Finish Line to change into for the Festival. 

Did You Come to Get Your Nuts Cracked?

Grab the official 2026 Arkansas Pecan Festival tee! Printed on soft, 100% cotton, lived-in Comfort Colors shirt in green. This year's festival tee is one you'll actually want to wear long after festival day.  

$30 each - Sizes S-XL

Pre-order yours and pick it up at the Pre-Ride Happy Hour at Moody Brews, Wednesday, December 2nd or on festival day, December 5th, in Keo. Last day to order a shirt is November 30th.

Ride Morning

  • Check-In: Look for the Keo Collective at the Airstrip. They’ll get you to the start line on the runway. *Note, there will be a single toilet available at the Airstrip, please plan accordingly, extra facilities available a half mile west at the Festival.
  • Drop Bags: Write your name clearly on your bag and place any post-ride clothes or gear inside. Volunteers will transport it to the official Finish Line in downtown Keo at the Arkansas Pecan Festival. 

Finish Line Celebration

The ride officially ends in Keo, right in the heart of the Arkansas Pecan Festival. Secure your bike in the secure bike area, grab a Moody Brews pour, and savor your well-earned slice of pecan pie. Stick around to enjoy the festival’s car show, vendors, entertainment, and holiday cheer.

Important Note: You must register before November 23 to guarantee your slice of pie is reserved for you at the Finish Line.

After the Festival

When you’ve had your fill of pie and fun, noodle back at your own pace to the Keo Airstrip to retrieve your vehicle. Don’t forget to collect your drop bag with your kit, helmet, and shoes before heading out.

EventName: The Sandy Neck Fat Bike Winter Classic!
EventNotes:
Please Sign the online waiver!

PLEASE READ!!! 

EVERY QUESTION IS ANSWERED HERE!

After you are registered be sure to join this Strava Club: https://www.strava.com/clubs/466019/members.

 The Sandy Neck Fat Bike Winter Classic (SNFBWC) is back for a fun time!

 Way back when we first had this idea; to race Fat Bikes on Sandy Neck Beach in December we didn’t know it would double in size and still sell out so fast.

It's been sold out since 2019, so you know we are going to do something new to commemorate it. Funny apparel is encouraged.

The 2026 edition of our 15-mile party ride will follow nearly the same route as last year - zigzagging back and forth across Sandy Neck, out to the Lighthouse and back to the parking lot. 

 - START TIME IS NOON.  

 Online registration only. Check in begins at 10:30am on race day.

 Ride begins at noon with a mass start roll out on the beach. We expect all participants to finish and safely exit the Sandy Neck course by 3:30pm, long before the sun sets. If you think it will take you longer than 3-½ hours to complete, please tell an official at registration.

 All riders will be checked in at the beginning and, more importantly, MUST BE CHECKED OUT at the end of the course, because everybody has to be accounted for before the volunteers and Sandy Neck Ranger Staff can finish their day and join the after party and we don’t want to lose anybody!

 The lighthouse aid station will include a water bubbler for refilling your water bottles, cookies or brownies, and maybe more. Note that the lighthouse is on private property, so we can have all kinds of fun. The aid station will close at 2:30pm. Again: Everybody has to be off the race course by 3:30pm and checked off by a race official as having safely completed the ride. 

 If you want to compete for a prize: the race component of this party ride is a sprint starting 100 yards or so from the race start and ending on the beach just before you get to the lighthouse. This is also the first of two Strava segments (https://www.strava.com/segments/30358128).

 Since that’s it for racing, you’re welcome to hang out at the Lighthouse longer and have more fun!

 The second segment will stay up for bragging rights but will not be part of the race. It starts after exiting the lighthouse driveway and ends 100 yards or so before the Sandy Neck Gatehouse, which is the end of the race and where you will be checked off by an official (https://www.strava.com/segments/30358166). 

 Winners of the sprint will be determined by a race official at the finish line. Small prizes will go to the top three women and top three men.

 Intersections will be clearly marked with arrows and/or race tape. While the elevation on this route is minimal, the challenge is grinding through several long stretches of deep, sugary sand. There are few short walk up ascents and a bunch of exciting but short descents.

 All proceeds for SNFBWC will benefit the Cape Cod chapter of NEMBA (https://nemba-capecod.org/).

 All participants are required to wear a helmet and carry phones with ringers on in case of emergency and to help us account for you if you aren’t checked off at race end for whatever reason. 

 

Directions to the start: 
From 6A in East Sandwich, follow Sandy Neck Road past the Gatehouse to the main parking lot at the end of the road. 

The address is: Sandy Neck Beach, West Barnstable, MA 02668.

 

Post-ride party will be at a location (Off the Grid) and have a cash bar but dinner is included. Ther is a possability that 2 signature SNFBWC  beverages from Independent Fermentations Brewing will be picked up at registration.  All riders and volunteers get a newly designed 2026 commemorative item.

 

Party location: Off the Grid

91 MA-6A, Sandwich, MA 02563

 

 

 

Rain or Shine - No Refunds

 

Additional useful information:

At a casual pace, the route will take most people well under three hours. The race route is about 7 miles, short race=more hanging out time at the lighthouse.

Check the weather and dress appropriately.

The difficulty of the route is largely dependent on the temperature and the moisture content of the sand. 

There are a half dozen or so challenging but short hike-a-bikes.

Bailouts are permitted as long as you check out at the end, but the route is only 15 miles and we encourage you to ride the whole thing.

A Sandy Neck ranger and a bicycle mechanic will follow the race in case there are any situations requiring assistance.

No tire size regulations - ride whatever you want. However, the Town of Barnstable prohibits Ebikes on Sandy Neck. 

We recommend lowering your tire pressure, depending on your weight, to 4 to 6 PSI, or, as low as you can go without hitting your rims.

Pre-Ride:  https://www.strava.com/routes/2893178626970685656. NOTE:  The section from Trail 6 around the point of Sandy Neck to the Lighthouse is only permissible on race day. When you see a ‘No Bikes’ sign, respect it and continue on the main trail. This is a very special day, the one time a year we get to ride around the point to the Sandy Neck Lighthouse!

Categories.CategoryName: 6 Hour Team - 3-4 Person Teams NICA Youth Only

EventNotes:
Register now to be part of the best XC Endurance event in Oklahoma - Dam Zombies (4 season).  Choose your adventure: 3 Hour Solo, 6 Hour Solo or 6 Hour Team. This year we are adding special NICA categories to allow for our youth to compete against each other on their own separate course. What's more is a NICA Family Team category - where a NICA Athlete and adult (coach, mentor, parent) can team up and compete with other NICA Family teams.   NICA and Non-NICA will only share the pit zone and start finish trails - no overlapping the single track for Veteran Zombies and Fresh Zombies (NICA). By popular demand, I've added an e-bike category; e-bikes will race the non-NICA course with the other “veteran zombies." 

What to expect: Line up at 10:00 for the 6-hour mass start, or 1:00 for the 3-hour solo mass start. Ride as many complete laps as you can within the 3 or 6 hours. The winner is the most laps within the time limits. Tied for laps? The winner is the who completed their full laps first (fastest clock time).  Take as many breaks as you like to rest or fuel up, get maintenance done, or switch out a bike (don't forget to move your number plate). Teams - Only one team member riding the course at a time. Team members can rotate as often as you like (each lap, every few laps or half the race - you decide). Only catch is each team member must ride a minimum of one lap. 

The Pit Zone - set up your team tent, grab some hot pancakes for a donation from the NICA grill. Stick around for the end of the race for complimentary BBQ. All registrants will receive a custom I Survived Dam Zombies long sleeve tee. Custom trophies for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place for all categories.  Out on the course Gearhead Outfitters will be providing neutral support Skratch Hydration - grab a cup on the go or stop and fill up your bottle. 

The Dam Zombies never disappoints - be sure to be one of the first 100 to register to claim one of the awesome custom shirts. 

 

- Turbo Joe (event director)

EventName: Capital `Cross Classic -- Event #8 of the 2026 BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series and MABRA Cat Champs
EventNotes:
The Bike Lane Presents

2026 Capital `Cross Classic Cyclocross Race

To Benefit Trails in Lake Fairfax Park

Finals of the 2026 BikeReg Super Series and MABRA Category Champs

Sunday, December 6, 2026, Lake Fairfax Park, Reston, VA

 

General Info

The 2026 Capital ‘Cross Classic is a USAC cyclocross event. All USAC rules and penalties apply. As the rider, you are responsible for knowing the rules for the race in which you are racing.

Beneficiary: Proceeds will benefit the Lake Fairfax Sustainable Natural Trail System program, which aims to build new sustainable trails and restore existing trails in Lake Fairfax Park.


Venue and amenities: The Capital Cross Classic course is located on the grounds of Lake Fairfax Park in Reston, Va. Heated restrooms, food vendor, a beer garden and free drinking water will be available onsite throughout the day. Alcohol is prohibited in the park, except in designated areas. There is a children’s playground located near the racecourse. As the event is a benefit for the park’s trails, attendees are encouraged to explore the miles of trails available in the park during their visit.

Parking: Parking is available in lots located off Lake Fairfax Drive in the park. Parking is free, IF course conditions are dry. However, the promoter reserves the right to institute a mandatory $2/vehicle parking fee if the course is soft or muddy and could suffer significant damage during the event. Capital ‘Cross Classic is a benefit for trail building and maintenance and it is the goal of the promoters to leave no trace of our use of the park. All damage to the park [turf, etc] will be paid for with proceeds from the race. If a parking fee is instituted, those funds will only be used to repair the course and/or benefit trails. Announcements regarding a parking fee will be made on the BikeReg.com registration page prior to the race. All racers and other attendees are encouraged to bring $2/vehicle to the race, just in case.

Team Parking: Team parking is available in close proximity to the racecourse. Please contact the promoter no later than one week in advance for team parking reservations. Team parking spots will be offered on a first-come-first-served basis.

Warm-ups: For the safety and courtesy of all racers, warming up on the course during races is prohibited. Violators will be disqualified. The course will be open for warm-ups during the 15 minutes preceding each race, if no racers remain on course.

Staging Procedure: Riders will fill the starting grid by bib number, 8 riders at a time, as specified in the USA Cycling Cyclocross rulebook when so directed by the officials; the officials will fill any gaps left by DNS or late-arriving riders as appropriate. All riders must assemble in the pre-staging chute no later than 10 minutes before their start. Riders arriving late to staging will be staged at the back of the starting grid.

Call-ups: You MUST pre-register if you want a call-up. For categories that award series points, the first 8 bibs (i.e., the front row) will be assigned to the top 8 pre-registered riders on series points.  Remaining pre-registered riders will be staged by CrossResults ranking.  Late/day-of riders will be staged by bib number, in the order of registration. The Men Cat. 5 and Women Cat. 4/5 categories will be staged by entry date & time for pre-registered riders, followed by late/day-of riders in the order of registration.  All categories will reserve four spots in the third row, which are to be used for promoters' discretionary call-ups.

Barrier Primes: Prizes will be awarded to the first rider in each field to clear the barriers cleanly on the first lap. For combined fields or fields that start simultaneously, one winner will be determined for that group. Winners MUST report immediately to the finish/podium area to claim their prizes. This will take place immediately after you finish. Failure to do so will result in a forfeit of your prize. Primes will be judged by race staff, not USA Cycling officials.

Series Points: Points are awarded for BikeReg Super Series rankings for all categories except Men Cat. 4 and Women Cat. 4/5.

Podium Finishers: The top finishers in every event MUST report immediately to the finish/podium area for awards and interviews. This will take place immediately after you finish and only last a few minutes. Failure to do so will result in a forfeit of your prizes.

BikeReg Super Series Top Finishers: Capital ‘Cross Classic is the series final for the BikeReg Super Series.

This event is held under USA Cycling permit 16497, pending.  

Course Info

The course is roughly 3km in length and consists of a paved start, grass and hard pack terrain, gravel paths, climbs, descents and some off-camber turns. The course will feature both man-made and natural obstacles.

Registration, Scoring, and Schedule

License: a USA Cycling racing license is required for entry in all fields except Li'l Belgians.  Unlicensed riders will be assessed an additional $15 in their shopping cart for a Beginner 1-Day license during registration.  Unlicensed riders may only register for fields that are specifically identified as "1-Day license valid for entry."  Racing Age for Cyclocross is defined as the rider's age on December 31, 2027.

Entry Fees:  The pre-registration entry fee is $40 for adult races and $20 for Junior races.  Online registration by BikeReg.com.  Online registration closes Fri., December 4, 2026 at 8:30 AM.  BikeReg assesses a service charge for online registration. There are no refunds and no mail-in registration.    

This page will re-open for late registration in the afternoon of the Friday prior to the event.  Late entry fees will increase to $50 for adults and $25 for Juniors.  All sales will be conducted through BikeReg – there will be no in-person sales at the event.  Register at home on Saturday or Sunday before coming out, or on your phone at the event.

Additional entries are priced at $20 during the pre-registration period, and the discount is applied automatically if the entries are purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart.  For additional entries purchased separately, use the ‘Contact Us’ link at the bottom of this page to request a partial refund.  During the late registration period and on race day, additional entries are priced at $25.  A coupon will be made available at the day-of registration table for additional entries purchased separately, to achieve the discounted price.

Race-day Check-In:  Race day check-in and late entry will open by 7:30 AM, and closes 20 minutes prior to the start of the first race in each time slot; the closing time will be strictly enforced.  Plan your arrival at the venue accordingly, and don't wait for the last possible minute to check in. 

Complimentary Entries: Current National Cyclocross Champions shall be granted a free entry but must wear a national jersey in the class which it was won. All candidates for complimentary entries must be settled with the promoter no less than one week in advance. Complimentary race entry will be given to the 2025 Super Series winners of the following fields: Men Cat 1/2/3; Women Cat 1/2/3.

Event held rain or shine. In the event of severe weather please refer to the race website for up to date info.

Directions

The race is held in Reston, Virginia at Lake Fairfax park - Google Map address; 1400 Lake Fairfax Dr - Reston, VA 20190

From the Capitol Beltway (I-495): Exit onto the Dulles Toll Road (Rt. 267). Pay toll. Travel on the toll road for 6 miles and then take Exit 14 onto Hunter Mill Road. Pay toll. Turn right at the traffic light and travel on Hunter Mill for 2 miles. Turn left at the first traffic light onto Baron Cameron Avenue. Travel on Baron Cameron for 0.1 miles and then turn left at the first intersection onto Lake Fairfax Drive. Take the road into the park and follow signs to race parking.

The Bike Lane bicycle shop is one of the area's full service bike shops and a supplier of cyclocross bikes and parts. The Bike Lane strives to educate the public on bicycle safety and advocate for bicycle safe communities. It also gives back to our community.

In the event of a medical emergency there will be an ambulance on site, provided by the Dunn Loring Volunteer Fire Dept., for the duration of the event. If the emergency is life threatening or otherwise a very serious matter the closest Hospital is the Reston INOVA hospital located here:

EventNotes:
Kelley Acres Speed Shop

2026 Fall Performance Training

8-Week Program 

Please read the information below carefully before selecting your in-person or at-home training option.

 

Program Overview

The 8-week Fall Performance Training Program begins the week of October 11, 2026  and ends the week of December 10, 2026

 

The Fall session follows a progressive training plan focused on improving pedaling efficiency, cycling-specific skills, and intensity management. Each week builds upon the previous week to prepare athletes for the 2027 Winter Performance Training Program.

Tuesday Night Words:  High-Intensity Advanced Training

Wednesday: Speed-Focused Training

Thursday: Strength-Focused Training

Athletes who register for two in-person classes per week will receive a $45 discount.

Equipment Information

A cadence display on your bike computer is recommended. KASS cadence sensors may be available for use.

Important: KASS uses wheel-on trainers. If your bike has a thru axle, you must bring a compatible trainer thru-axle adapter.

Visit The Robert Axle Project for compatibility information.

Please bring:

  • Your bike

  • A water bottle

  • A towel—or two if you sweat heavily!

  • A heart-rate monitor is also recommended

KASS At-Home Training

The KASS At-Home option allows you to complete the Fall Performance Training workouts on your own schedule.

Two complementary workouts will be offered each week:

  • Speed Demon: Speed-focused training

  • Beast Mode: Strength-focused training

The workouts target different energy systems and are designed to work together as part of a balanced, progressive training plan.

The at-home workout package is $90 and includes [Speed Demon, Beast Mode, or both—PLEASE CONFIRM].

Workout files are available in the following formats:

  • .zwo for Zwift

  • .mrc for compatible training platforms

Workout files will be emailed each Monday.

Athletes are responsible for uploading the files and confirming compatibility with their chosen training platform. If you experience technical problems, please contact the support team for that platform.

Zwift: Importing Custom Workouts

TrainerRoad Support

Additional class information is available at www.kelleyacres.net.

Schedule Notes

There will be no classes during Thanksgiving week 11/23/2026. This is a scheduled recovery week.

Classes may occasionally be canceled because of inclement weather. Riders will be notified by email and will receive the scheduled workout to complete at home.

Registration Policies

Because each registration reserves a limited space in the program, registration fees are generally non-refundable once the session begins.

Missed classes are not refundable or eligible for a make-up class. An athlete may find a substitute and arrange reimbursement directly with that person.

If an injury prevents an athlete from completing the program, please contact KASS as soon as possible to discuss whether a transfer, credit, or other accommodation may be available.

If KASS cancels a class because of inclement weather, riders will be notified by email and will receive the scheduled workout to complete at home.

Join us for a focused 3-day block of structured Zwift training, live coaching, and online clinics designed to help you build fitness, sharpen your training approach, and start the next phase of your season with purpose.

Each morning runs from 9 a.m. to Noon (EDT), with plenty of interaction between CCNS coaches and fellow campers along the way. Expect hard work, useful feedback, and the kind of supportive group environment that makes training better.

What to Expect from vCamp

  • A pre-camp one-on-one goals review and power-profile analysis.
  • Three days of purposeful training designed to challenge your fitness and give us useful insight into your strengths and opportunities.
  • Live coaching, accountability, and the motivation of training alongside other committed athletes.
  • Informative clinics covering training, nutrition, race preparation, tactics, and performance.
  • Real-time coaching and tactical guidance during selected Zwift sessions.

Meet Your Coaches

Overview

Every athlete comes into camp with different goals, but each day follows a similar rhythm:

  • Riding starts at 9 a.m. EST
  • Pre-ride briefing covering the day's objectives, workout, route, and key coaching points.
  • Time on bike is generally 2.5-2.75 hours. Don't worry, we take breaks throughout to stretch and resupply!
  • Post-ride communication comes later in the day, featuring notable results and instructions for the next day.

CCNS vCamp Requirements

A few basic technical requirements help us make vCamp as interactive and useful as possible. Need assistance getting set up? We'll help you.

#1: vCamp athletes must be able to communicate through Zoom during the training window.

#2: You must have access to a browser or secondary device separate from your Zwift display for clinics, presentations, and other camp content.

#3: Daily attendance matters. vCamp is designed as a complete 3-day training block, and the value comes from participating consistently from day to day. Please plan to be ready and online before each day's scheduled start.

Your First Steps

Step 1: Register for the vCamp that fits your schedule. January's vCamp is here.

Step 2: If you are not a current CCNS athlete, schedule your pre-camp call with a CCNS coach so we can review your riding, goals, and current fitness.

That's it! 
You're on your way to three productive days of riding, learning, and building momentum for the season ahead.

Want to Learn More?

Wondering what the daily training will look like or which clinic topics we'll cover?
Email us at vCamp@charlescoaching.com for a detailed camp overview and answers to any questions you may have.

EventName: The Ride Series MTB Skills Clinics: Florida Markham Park Dec 12/13
EventNotes:
Whether you're just getting started, looking to gain confidence on trail, wanting to unlock more speed and flow, or preparing for race day, The Ride Series Florida MTB Skills Experience offers a progression-based approach to becoming a more capable and confident rider.

Choose the session that best fits where you are in your riding journey—or build your own progression by attending multiple sessions throughout the event. Using The Ride Series' proven coaching methodology, each clinic breaks down mountain bike skills into clear, understandable movements and then puts those skills into action on the trail.

From building a strong foundation, to finding flow through jumps and features, to developing the skills that can help you ride faster and race smarter, these sessions are designed to give riders the tools they need to progress.

Three sessions. One goal: help you ride with more confidence, control, and momentum.

The Ride Series Foundations

Build the skills that make everything else easier.

The Foundations session is designed for beginner and intermediate riders who want to develop greater confidence, control, and efficiency on the bike. We'll break down the essential movements that create a strong platform for better riding and apply them to real trail situations.

Topics may include:

  • Body position and balance
  • Braking control
  • Cornering fundamentals
  • Looking ahead and line choice
  • Managing roots, obstacles, and uneven terrain
  • Building confidence on the trail

This is the perfect starting point for riders who want to better understand why certain techniques work—not just be told what to do.

Ideal for: Beginner to intermediate riders.

Florida Flow

More momentum. More confidence. More fun.

Florida Flow is all about learning how to use your bike and the terrain to create speed, confidence, and flow. Whether you're working toward your first jump, becoming more comfortable with drops, or learning how to carry momentum through features, this session will help you better understand the movements behind it all.

We'll focus on building skills progressively and meeting riders where they are, creating opportunities to challenge yourself without simply being told to "send it."

Topics may include:

  • Pumping and generating speed
  • Managing pressure and preload
  • Jump fundamentals and progression
  • Drops and feature management
  • Carrying momentum
  • Linking features together
  • Building confidence in the air

Ideal for: Intermediate and progressing riders looking to develop more flow, confidence, and feature skills.

The Ride Series XC Race Prep Clinic

Ride smarter. Carry more speed. Find your free speed.

The Ride Series XC Race Prep Clinic is designed for riders who want to translate solid skills into better performance on race day. This isn't a fitness clinic—it's about developing the technical efficiency, confidence, and decision-making that can help you carry more momentum and make better use of your fitness on the trail.

We'll focus on the moments that can make a difference when the clock is running: braking, cornering, line choice, acceleration, technical features, and maintaining control when fatigue starts to set in.

Topics may include:

  • Efficient body position for speed and control
  • Carrying momentum through corners
  • Braking less and braking smarter
  • Line choice and trail strategy
  • Managing roots, rough terrain, and technical sections
  • Passing and race-specific decision making
  • Applying skills under pressure and fatigue

Whether you're preparing for your next NICA race, local XC event, enduro, or simply want to ride faster and more efficiently, this session is designed to help you discover where your free speed is hiding.

Ideal for: Intermediate to advanced riders and racers.

EventName: DragonSlayer 2026 Presented by Georgetown Trails Foundation.
EventNotes:
Georgetown Trails Foundation and EnduraRace Trails present the annual DragonSlayer!  DS2026

What started as 3 laps for a 78 mile event in 2017 still occurs on the gnarly rock gardens of Goodwater Trail around Lake Georgetown but now, as of 2019, utilizes the 30 mile loop option for more mileage per lap.

This event has achieved mythic status over the years as one of the hardest mountain-bike single day events in the country with up to 15 hours needed to complete the 100 miles, but with bail-out distances of 30, 60, and 90 miles available. 

In addition to the classic format, we've upped the ante further and created the hands-down most wicked ride ever with a 200 mile, 36-hour category called The DragonSlayer Legendary.  Can anyone even finish this monster? It may only happen once or once every few years, so don't miss out!

THE ROUTE:

The DragonSlayer uses all of the 26 mile traditional Goodwater loop with the addition of four extra miles to add up to the 30 mile distance. See the 2019 route below. It's the same for 2026.

In the past, all laps were in one direction for the given year. This time around, you will ride in “washing-machine” style. That is, your first lap will be clockwise, second lap counter-clockwise, third lap clockwise, and so on. This should add a social element to the event as you can watch each other slowly degrade into base elements over the course of the weekend. The 10 mile kickers for the 100 and 200 distances are always counter-clockwise from the start finish to a sign that tells you to “turn around”. Yes, just like the Bonnie Tyler song. 

Where it says “ranger station” on the map: what that means is there is a hut with no one inside to hear your complaint. There is however a water spigot on the back of these you can use to wash the blood and dirt off with or refill water too. They also make a good landmark for someone to find you if you phoned a friend for a rescue.

RULES:

  1. 180 spots for the Classic and 20 spots for the Legendary. I may change this around based on demand.
  2. No e-bikes allowed on USACE parkland and thus no e-bikes allowed in this event.
  3. Riders of the 200 mile Legendary MUST start at 8pm on Friday 12/18/2026 and MUST finish before 8am Sunday 12/20/2026 to be considered a finisher. Additionally, they must finish 90 miles (3 laps) by noon Saturday 12/19/2026 (16 hours) or be disqualified and dropped down to the Classic. If they make the noon cut off, they will then have 20 hours to finish the remaining 110 miles which includes two 10 mile out-and-back kickers. They may ride their kickers anytime they wish, including in the opening three laps, but must have a full three laps completed by noon, kickers not withstanding, on Saturday to continue, so they should plan their time carefully. Riders of the 200 can bail at any completed lap distance and will qualify for the appropriate distance reward listed below.
  4. Riders of the 90 and 100 mile Classic distances MUST start at 8am on Saturday 12/19/2026 and finish by 11pm 12/19/2026 to be considered a finisher (15 hours). They must also start their final lap BEFORE 6pm Saturday 12/19/2026. Riders of the 100 in addition to three 30 mile laps, must also complete their 10 mile out-and-back kicker before time expires at 11pm Saturday 12/19/2026. They can ride their kicker at any point during the event, but MUST start their final full lap before 6pm.
  5. Riders seeking the 30 or 60 mile lesser distances may start at 8am, but must start before 1pm on Saturday 12/19/2026 and be off-course by 11pm Saturday 12/19/2026. They must also start their final lap BEFORE 6pm Saturday 12/19/2026. There is a 10 hour cut-off for 30 and 60 mile distance credit.
  6. Anyone starting a lap after 2pm must have a helmet light and a bar light. It is recommended they have a set of backup lights too for safety whether its 2pm or not. Plan for needing up to six hours of lights for a lap.
  7. There will be a sweep rider for the Classic which will hit the trail after the last person has started their final lap. There may be a sweep rider for the Legendary as well if anyone lasts long enough to even start a final lap.
  8. Riders are allowed to pre-stage food, water, and supply caches along the route, but are wholly responsible for cleaning them up after their event within 12 hours of their finish. Likewise, there is no protection or guarantee that such caches will not be raided by other park users, animals, or participants, so consider how to label, lock and/or conceal them if that is a concern.
  9. Riders can accept outside aid as long as they, their supplies, and their bike progress along the prescribed route 100% under their own power.  Thus first aid, food, water, mechanical assistance, etc. may all be delivered by a support person along the route, but that aid cannot in any way physically advance the rider, their supplies, or their bike forward.
  10. Riders can leave the course and return, by the shortest available route and by any means available, to the start/finish for first aid, mechanical/break-down repair, etc. reasons BUT must return to the exact point where they left the course to continue their event if they wish to do so. Time cut offs are still in effect. They must have GPS tracking verification available after the event to prove they picked up where they left off.
  11. Riders can switch bikes during the event as well as Frankenstein together anything that they can pedal under their own power and can borrow parts or even full bikes from others.
  12. Riders can help other riders on course apart from physically moving them, their bikes, or supplies forward. So mechanical help is fine, pushing someone's bike or carrying them or their pack for them is not. That is a disqualifier (perhaps they are too injured or drained to continue anyway) for the person accepting the help. You can loan out certain things you are carrying though such as water, food, backup lighting, tubes, sealant, or other spare parts however without it being a disqualifier even though the person being helped are technically now carrying such for you.
  13. All riders MUST ride with a GPS tracker AND with a charged cell-phone. Riders must be prepared upon request to show the GPS record of their ride in order to receive credit.  Riders will be asked to send a link of their GPS tracker link to the organizer so he may keep track of where you are during your ride both for your safety, schedule planning, and for accountability. Backup battery chargers are encouraged.
  14. All riders MUST CHECK IN before starting each new lap or kicker so we know to keep track of you if you go missing.
  15. All riders abandoning their ride MUST notify the organizer by email, text, or in person before they leave the event.
  16. All participants, riders or spectators, must sign a waiver online through bike-reg or in person at check-in.
  17. Absolutely no sales for products or services of any kind at allowed by the USACE on parkland other than offering donations for camping to help defray the rental fee for the two group shelters.
  18. All pets must be on a leash at all times and all pet waste must be collected and properly disposed of by owner.
  19. Pack it in and pack it out. Leave no trash behind please.
  20. No drinking from glass containers in the park. You can pour into a tumbler and then carefully dispose of the glass bottle.

 

THE SCHEDULE:

Friday 12/18/2026 3pm set-up.

Friday 12/18/26 6pm-7:30pm check-in for all distances. 

Friday 12/18/2026 Riders meeting at 7:45pm and planned 8pm DragonSlayer Legendary 200 starts.

Saturday 12/19/2026 6am-7:30am check-in for DragonSlayer Classic

Saturday 12/19/2026 Riders meeting at 7:45am and planned 8am DragonSlayer Classic starts for all distances (if only planning to do one or two laps, start before noon).

SATURDAY 12/19/2026 11pm DragonSlayer Class cut-off time (or at 15 hours). Finish late by even 1 second and it does not count!

SUNDAY 12/20/2026 8am DragonSlayer Legendary cut-off time (or at 36 hours). Finish 1 second late? No credit.

Pack up and leave a trash free park by 10am Sunday.

The organizer reserves the right to actually sleep on occasion during what for them is a 40+ hour event, so please try to self-manage off hours.

AWARDS:

The 2026 DragonSlayer is not a race (though time is kept and published). The goal is to finish. That's it…just finish. Trust me, that's enough. Once you are out there for multiple laps you will realize that is not very easy especially for the longer distances.  The DragonSlayer is about you versus the trail, you versus the weather, you versus your mind telling you to quit, sometimes you versus your bicycle that refuses to cooperate, and often times all of the above. Finishing is quite the award in and of itself. But we have some DragonSlayer traditional awards to provide as well:

30 mile (1 lap) - BabyDragon distance. We will encourage you to train for next year to do 60+ miles.

60 miles (2 lap) - DragonMaster rock trophy

90 miles (3 laps) - DragonSlayer rock trophy

100 miles (3 laps plus kicker) - DragonSlayer rock trophy plus 100 mile buckle until they run out.

200 miles (6 laps plus 2 kickers) - DragonSlayer Legendary rock trophy, 100 mile buckle until they run out, plus a dragon-themed commemorative sword (it's a real sword).

A note on the rocks…Tradition is that on your last lap, you choose your rock though sometimes your rock chooses you. It should be at least the size of a large baking potato and the more gnarly it is as Swiss-cheese limestone, the better. Haul your rock with you on your last lap and bring it to the organizer to get marked up. That is your trophy, and you will treasure it for the rest of your life. Your rock does not necessarily have to be from the Georgetown area, but if it is not, it should have some special significance for you and at least be potato-sized.

We will also be getting jersey designs together for finishers to order on their own nickel as in years past. The jerseys are designed according to the distance you achieved. Yes the Legendary jersey will be…well…Legendary.

Jerseys from 2018 and on:

NUMBER PLATES AND CHIP TIMING:

We use a Race-Result timing system which has a antenna mat you ride over to record time events.  There is no promise, warranty, or guarantee that timing will work perfectly as this is not a race, but we are pretty good at timing, so that would be unforeseen. Chip timing can do funny things after the clock strikes midnight, so for the Legendary, it is more of an automated check-in device than anything else.

DragonSlayer Legendary riders get a specific number plate that lets everyone know what they signed up for and may imply that they are completely insane for doing so. 

DragonSlayer Classic riders get their own version of the number plate which will still be hard-core as they have all been in the past.

Register by November 16th and you will get a number plate with your name on it. I will even let you choose your 3-digit or less number first come first serve. Use the event contact form to request your number.

All plates will include a single RF chip attached with 3m adhesive on the back. I would encourage you throw an additional level of packing tape over this as the race is so brutal, we have had chips dislodge before.

If you show up wanting to ride using your TMBRA plate or anything else other than the DS2026 plate, you will be criminally trespassed and banished from the event for a period of no less than 99 years with no refunds.

PARKING:

Park along Park Road 8 which is the left turn after entering the park. There will be some traffic cones and signs and perhaps an eager volunteer (6am to 8am) to direct you there. PARK ON THE RIGHT HAND SIDE OFF THE GRASS, all wheels/tires on pavement, in a line, bumper to bumper as you enter as close as you can to the Cul-de-Sac without parking in the Cul-de-Sac unless you are a volunteer or event staff. You will ride past your car twice a lap along Park Road 8 making it easy to re-supply.

The main parking lot as you enter the park gate is available as overflow though we've never needed it in the past. Park Road 8 is a half mile long.

We will hold vehicle traffic on Park Road 8 five minutes before and after the mass starts for the Legendary and for the Classic or until the entire peloton is onto the trails.

START/FINISH AND AID STATION:

The start/finish line is at the end of Park Road 8 in the Cul-de-Sac along with basic bathrooms, water jugs, packet pick-up, first-aid (very minimal), and bike wash.  

There are more water jugs on the other side of the lake at the Westlake Parkway trail-head. 

Water is also available via spigots at Camp Tejas, Hogg, Overlook, and Cedar Breaks parks. 

There are additional trail-side bathrooms at Camp Tejas and Overlook. Cedar Breaks as well, but they are well off-course.

 

CAMPING/LODGING:

Primitive tent/car camping is available at the start/finish area first come first serve. There are water spigots for drinking water and bike-wash, plugs for charging lights, and a couple of typical park-land restrooms available. 100 spots available for tents (parking your vehicle along park road 8 after dropping off your camping gear in the cul-de-sac area of the start/finish).  It is greatly appreciated if campers can donate towards the shelter rental fees to offset costs for the organizer. A QR code will be available onsite for this or you can send directly to @Todd-Galbraith-6 on Venmo.

There are improved and shelter campsites a short ride distance away at Russell Park which are available through the Lake Georgetown website (https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/234665)

The RV slips normally available a couple of miles away at Jim Hogg park will be closed for remodeling and construction. This update was received on 7/6/26. Plan accordingly if you were planning to “glamp”.

There are also campsites at Camp Tejas (https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/234643) and Cedar Breaks (https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/232544?tab=campsites) but these are much much further away.

 

WEATHER:

The event will occur rain or shine, within reason. The event is insured for inclement weather that would create a significant hazard for riders and/or significant trail damage in the opinion of the organizer. This means you could still have to ride in some amount of rain, cold, heat, etc. If this is a concern, consider purchasing your own event insurance. A lot can happen in a 36 hour event window, so be prepared.

INSURANCE:
The event will be covered by the required amount of insurance provided by OBRA/NOBRA to satisfy the USACE. Participants will sign a waiver and be expected to handle all their own medical bills, or other costs associated with this event. 

DISCLAIMER:

The Goodwater trail is an unforgivingly brutal test of bike handling skills, endurance, and strength. It is a 30 mile loop of which 20 is rock-garden to include about 2000 vertical feet of climbing per lap. It is a very difficult trail. Participants should not attempt unless they have pre-ridden the lap to first know what they are in for. They should likewise train for their distance goals. Sturdy bikes and strong tires are a requirement to finish and even the best will at times break. 

Participants are expected to self-rescue. You can call the start/finish and we can assist with calling 911 to your location, but your ultimate survival whether in success or failure solely resides in your own hands. 

 

ABOUT OUR SPONSORS:

The Georgetown Trail Foundation is dedicated to planning, building, maintaining, and advocacy of mountain bike and hiking trails in the Georgetown area. The famous Katy trail is their masterpiece and thanks to their hard work, more and more land is being set aside for additional trails in the future.

EnduraRace Trails, formerly just EnduraRace, is headed up by the race organizer  known as Todd Eric who is also known for timing, race promotion and event management for mountain races across Texas and Arkansas. He is also an accomplished trail designer and builder whose current capstone work is the Forrest Creek Ranch trail which has been described as “sacred geometry” in terms of carefully built flow for maximum speed and fun.  He plans to work some trail building in soon for both Lakeway and Georgetown as his day-job schedule allows.

More sponsors to come we hope!

RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SUCCESS:

Ride your own pace and do not race. Don't blow up lap 1 trying to stay up with the pro-level riders or anyone else faster than you for that matter. Even if you are the slowest out there, you may still turn more miles than the faster riders in the end and take home the rock trophy they wanted but their ego stole from them. 

If you ride with a buddy, you need to ride to the lower common denominator and not push each other past the lessor's ability. Recognize though when it is time to tell your faster buddy to push on without you and let them take their best shot at their distance goal.

Plan your work and work your plan. Hydration and Nutrition coupled with realistic pacing goals are the key. Plan for 24oz of water with electrolyte mix (4-6oz sips at a time) and 300 calories (1 gel per 20 minutes) per hour max. Anymore than this and it blocks up your gut or washes out your electrolytes. Add protein to the mix after third hour and on to the end.  Save the caffeine for the final lap. Go sparingly on thick solid foods without a lot of water (24 oz/hr max).  

Keep a steady pace in the rocks with "light-hands" to keep the bike from bogging down. You need a solid 7mph average which means 5-6mph in the rocks and 10-12mph in the smooth. If a climb pushes you towards zone-4 heart rate, get off your bike and without a pause, walk the hill. At the top, get on and ride again immediately. Stay in zone 2 and 3 as much as you can.

Do not sleep unless you are SURE you can get going again after a short nap and keep your pit stops to 5 minutes or less barring repairs, etc. A 15 minute break can quickly become a 50 minute break and cost you your finish. Roll in, resupply, clean/oil chain and stanchions and leave for next lap. DO NOT SIT OR LAY DOWN if at all possible! Do not let your body think it is time to rest or that it is getting a rest. Remember when your body tells you it can do no more, you are only about 40% into it's full endurance capacity.

Hammer nutrition, pickle juice, Infinit, Tailwind, and other endurance racing products are fantastic for keeping you going but you have to TRAIN WITH THEM to know how your body responds to them. Do not try a new product the day of the DragonSlayer. Stick to the tried and true.

Pre-ride the course. Start now even if one lap is a struggle. Go out-and-back from each trailhead 5-10 miles each direction spread across several rides until you have the fitness to complete a full lap. Yes the trail needs some maintenance right now, but by the time of the event, it will be pristine if the weather cooperates.

Good Luck and keep the rubber side down!

Cyclocross Series Points System Official Scoring & Standings Rules for a 6-Race Series 

1. Series Overview: This scoring system provides a clear, competitive structure for a 6-race cyclocross series. It features a 25-point scale for the top-10 finishers, giving higher weight to podium positions while rewarding consistency down through 10th place. 

2. Per-Race Points Scale Placement Points Awarded;

 1st Place 25 pts, 2nd Place 20 pts, 3rd Place 16 pts, 4th Place 13 pts, 5th Place 10 pts, 6th Place 8 pts, 7th Place 6 pts, 8th Place 4 pts, 9th Place 2 pts, 10th Place 1 pt.

3. Series Rules & Regulations 

Best 5 out of 6 Races Count: Each rider's single lowest score (or missed race) is automatically dropped at the end of the series. This keeps standings competitive even if a rider experiences a mechanical failure, illness, or unavoidable absence.  Tiebreaker Protocol: If two or more riders are tied on total points after Race 6, ties will be resolved using the following hierarchy: 

1. Most 1st-place finishes in the series. 

2. Most 2nd-place finishes, 3rd-place finishes, etc. 

3. Higher finish position in the final race of the series (Race 6).

Program Director - Brad Huff

 

Membership Benefits

  • $250 annual membership fee
  • Each member receives:
    • Project Dudeman t-shirt
    • Project Dudeman cycling jersey or tech shirt
    • Supported weekly training rides with post-ride refreshments & gathering (March - Sept)

      • Wednesday - Wednesday Night Ride (WNR)

Why We’re Doing This.   
 

To create fun, fellowship, freedom, friendship, and fitness, while freeing ourselves from the stigma surrounding men’s mental health. Simply by sticking with our moto: “Just ride your bike, Dude!”

 

Show up, share the stoke, and trust that every pedal stroke is strengthening your resilience and sense of self.

 

More About Us

  • Not just a group ride, Project Dudeman is a commitment to presence—and a celebration of the rewards that come from honest effort.

  • We offer a renewed vision of what it means to be a man, rooted in slowing down, staying present, and honoring the moments that matter.

  • We ride with the understanding that perfection isn’t required—only authenticity. No one has to prove anything here. We ride to connect, not to conquer.

  • Average speed isn’t the goal. Consistency, quality, and shared experience are. That’s what builds real connection, confidence, and mental fitness—one ride at a time.

  • Accountability doesn’t come through force, rankings, or KOMs. It comes through presence, shared commitment, and living our code.

  • Project Dudeman is designed to supplement—not replace—your current riding group or club. Come experience how community and friendship can elevate not just your riding, but your life.

  • E-bikes are welcome. Always.

  • To put it simply:

    • Just ride your bike, Dude!

Are You Dudeman Material?

Too often, we fixate on the road right in front of us and miss the horizon of what’s possible.
Project Dudeman exists to change that.

We ride to broaden perspective—of potential, belief, and connection.

A bike teaches a simple truth: balance doesn’t come from standing still. Progress requires motion. Rigidity, ego, and force only slow the ride. Real progress is nurtured through resilience—by staying present, riding with intention, and moving forward with purpose.

Project Dudeman isn’t about perfection; it’s about placement. The right wheels, the right mindset, and the right people make all the difference. Like a peloton, we ride together—sitting in when we need to, taking a pull when we can. Our rides don’t burn us out; they clear the stress that clouds progress and reconnect us to ourselves and each other.

If this resonates, you’re already Dudeman material.

So clip in.
Take a pull when you can.
And remember—we’re all on this ride together.

Please read this!
 

Welcome to our FREE monthly ride! Ride start times vary by season to give us the best trail conditions and safest experience—May through September we roll out at 9:00 AM CT, and October through April we begin at 2:00 PM CT. We meet at the lower parking lot at Turkey Mountain Urban Wilderness Park, 6800 S Elwood Ave, Tulsa, OK 74132. Restrooms are available.

 

We will have ride leaders for skill levels between Beginner to Advanced. If you're new to mountain biking, OR have never taken WeROK’s Fundamentals, or other formal fundamentals skills clinics (even if you have been riding some), we REQUIRE YOU to start with the WeROK Fundamental Skills Session during registration. Regardless of your riding experience we feel taking this skills session will help improve your riding and create a better riding experience for all.

 

Loaner Bikes: Please refer to your registration confirmation letter. 
 

Cancellation/Bad Weather Policy: If bad weather develops we aim to cancel the event by 7:00 am the day of the ride.  Stay tuned to social media for announcements. We also follow Trailbot, in case Turkey Mountain trails are “closed” or “delayed”.  We do not have “rain dates”. 

 

Choosing appropriate group: First choose your riding and fitness level, then choose the best description among the groups. Once a group fills, the waitlist option will open. If you have a friend with the same skill level with whom you want to ride, help us out by registering together ASAP, in the same ride level, AND in same group number. Other than cancellations, we CANNOT GUARANTEE we can make any changes to groups, especially at the last minute, since we have group size restrictions. This delivers the best possible ride experience for all! If you don't end up riding with your friends, don't worry, you'll have the opportunity to make new ones!
 

Not sure which group to join? Ride levels are based on YOUR CURRENT skill and endurance levels. We want everyone to have the best and safest experience possible so we use a “rating” system to help align you with the right ride group. Please review the skills, endurance, mileage and proposed trails. Being in the right group makes a better, safer ride for all. If you are still unsure about which group might be for you just contact us at ride@werok.org. P.S. It is perfectly fine to “repeat” a level! Mastery of ALL levels takes time and practice. Please don’t rush yourself, nor succumb to peer pressure. NOTE: WeROK’s skill level names and colors are relative to Turkey Mountain trails. Other trail systems’ color designations could mean their Blue is (y)our Black, so be wise!
 

Advancing to next groups: A great way to know if you are ready to progress to the next ride level is if (1) you felt comfortable with skills necessary at your current level, and (2) you were able to keep up with the ride leader the entire ride and felt like you could have ridden longer. 

 

GROUP CHOICES:
 

1. FUNDAMENTAL SKILLS SESSION 

Select this group if you have never ridden a mountain bike, it’s been longer than you’d like to admit, OR you've never taken any type of basic mtb skills lessons before. Welcome! You have to start somewhere and this is the place! Even the most advanced riders should brush up on these essentials, and certainly, if you feel rusty, this session will help you. This session will cover the fundamentals of mountain biking, and then you'll hit the trail for a 2-3 mile ride. Successful completion of WeROK’s Fundamentals (or its equivalent) is required for advancement to next groups. Departure from this policy requires approval by a WeROK ride leader.

  • Skill Level: Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals are required (we may have loaner pedals available; email us ahead of time at ride@werok.org).
  • Skills you can perform: no requirement, you will definitely learn a skill or two after this session. 
  • Fitness Level: No requirement other than participate in possible heat for up to 2 hours.
  • Example of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, no rocks; double track near Bomb Cellar; the grassy fields; the Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop. 

2. FUNDAMENTALS TO GREEN Group

Select this group if you have taken the Fundamental Skills session, you feel more confident with those skills, and you are looking for a very easy-going transition to green trails. You will have a skills refresher for up to 15 minutes.

  • Skill Level: Confident Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals strongly encouraged (see above re: loaner pedals).
  • Skills you can perform: Staying upright while pedaling, skills learned in Fundamentals Group are beginning to make sense, and your confidence is growing.
  • Fitness Level: Completed a Fundamentals session with minimal fatigue
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with occasional flat, mellow rocks or roots, no significant downhill or uphill; Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop; the very first section of LoChi Connector.
  • Duration: 3-5 miles, maybe longer in cooler weather, no longer than 1.5 hours after refresher portion

3. GREEN Group
You’ve ridden on the dirt trails multiple times by now, and you’re getting the hang of things. You’re mastering the Fundamentals Skills, and your bike operating and handling skills feel smoother. No Fundamentals refresher portion provided.

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: Level pedals while coasting; one finger braking; becoming more comfortable with neutral and ready positions; and smoother corners/berms.
  • Fitness level: Able to ride steady at a comfortable pace for 30 minutes on easy terrain, and may need a breather while climbing, or at the top.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with a variety of low, smooth surface changes; more variety of up and downhill; LoChi; UHF or All Up with rests.
  • Duration: 5-7 miles,1.5 to 2.0 hours 

4. OPEN Group

Looking for new challenges! You are ready to explore more trail features (obstacles) and a variety of up and downhills, with limited stops. Mileage varies. No Fundamentals refresher provided. 

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus-to-Intermediate.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: GREEN skills are solid, but you’re out of saddle more instinctively with level pedals; in and out of neutral/ready position more smoothly; frequent appropriate shifting; smoother, smoother berms and corners; want to ride across straight bridges and skinnies 3-5 feet wide; comfortable choosing lines through rockier terrain, or between tight trees.
  • Fitness level: You’re riding a few times a week. Can ride a WeROK course continuously unless learning steep or more technical terrain. Pushing the pace uphill.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, more roots and rocks, twists and turns. The small bridge on OLD Lo Chi, All Up, UHF, Stay Gold Loop, Naharkey clockwise, maybe counterclockwise. Sessioning features within your skill set, such as the small skinny on Family Loop.
  • Duration: 8-10 miles, 2 hours with some stopping.

About USA Cycling and the NCNCA

USA Cycling (USAC) is the designated national governing body for the sport of cycling under the umbrella of the United States Olympic Committee (USOC). All Olympic sports follow the rules and regulations set forth in the USOC charter, and competitive cycling in the United States operates within this structure.

To better support riders, officials, promoters, and events across the country, USA Cycling divides the nation into regional districts. The Northern California Nevada Cycling Association (NCNCA) is the USA Cycling–recognized Local Association for the Northern California/Nevada region.

Whether you are new to the sport or a world-class athlete competing at the National, Pan American, World, or Olympic level, you participate within the support framework of USA Cycling, the USOC, and your Local Association — the NCNCA.

What the NCNCA Does

The NCNCA is a nonprofit, membership-based regional athletic association that supports competitive cycling and community-building across Northern California and Nevada. As the Local Association for USAC, the NCNCA is responsible for:

  • Coordinating and publishing the regional calendar of USA Cycling–sanctioned events
  • Supporting and training USA Cycling–licensed officials
  • Assisting promoters with event permitting and post-event reporting
  • Maintaining and providing event equipment to local promoters (finish-line cameras, timing equipment, traffic control gear, laptops, etc.)
  • Managing the region’s BAR/BAT season-long competition and race results
  • Supporting safety, fairness, and quality at all sanctioned events

The NCNCA’s ability to provide these services relies heavily on the support of its member clubs.

Membership and Club Support Levels

The NCNCA is governed by an elected Board of Directors. Member clubs contribute directly to the association’s annual operating budget. These contributions enable the NCNCA to maintain equipment, develop officials, run series competitions, support riders and promoters, and deliver high-quality racing experiences.

Clubs are invited to join at the following levels:

  • Gold Level – $500+
  • Silver Level – $250
  • Bronze Level – $150

All levels directly support the NCNCA’s mission: to maintain the highest standards of organization, safety, inclusion, development, and competition for riders, promoters, and the broader cycling community.

Membership Benefits by Support Tier

Membership-Wide Benefits (All Clubs)

Regardless of support tier, all NCNCA-affiliated clubs receive:

  • A comprehensive, year-round NCNCA event calendar with links to flyers, registration, and course maps
  • Conflict mitigation and scheduling coordination to maximize event success
  • Timely posting of results and standings for BAR/BAT and development series
  • Monthly newsletter and regular communication through social media and email
  • Oversight, rule enforcement, and the presence of trained officials at permitted events
  • A regional network that promotes safe, fair, and well-organized competition across all disciplines

These baseline services are funded by club contributions, USA Cycling Local Association support, grants, and volunteer effort.

Our Commitment

The NCNCA exists to support its members — riders, clubs, promoters, officials, and the cycling community at large. Our mission is to deliver a positive, inclusive, and high-quality cycling experience for athletes of every level.

Your team’s participation and financial support make this work possible. Together we can continue to grow and strengthen cycling in Northern California and Nevada.
